To fill the gap, we introduce SpatialVec, a boundary-aware spatial representation learning framework that adaptively samples geometry boundaries and their surrounding regions, capturing fine-grained geometric structures critical for topology-aware spatial reasoning. A transformer-based encoder-decoder trained through geometry reconstruction produces compact, geometry-aware, and unified representations for points, polylines, and polygons. Empirical evaluation on two real-world datasets shows that SpatialVec substantially improves the preservation of challenging topological relationships involving polygonal interactions and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines significantly on downstream prediction and classification tasks.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data as a full research paper

Multimedia.title: Self-Learning Surprise Detection in Spatial Audio for Viewport-Aware 360-Video Streaming
Multimedia.summary: Adaptive streaming of 360-degree video relies on viewport prediction to allocate bandwidth efficiently. Current approaches predominantly use visual saliency or historical gaze patterns, neglecting the role of spatial audio in guiding user attention. This paper presents a self-learning framework for detecting "surprising" auditory events, moments that deviate from learned temporal expectations, and demonstrates their utility for viewport prediction. The proposed architecture combines SE(3)-equivariant graph neural networks with recurrent temporal modeling, trained via a dual self-supervised objective. A key feature is the natural modeling of temporal attention decay: surprise is high at event onset but diminishes as the listener adapts. Experiments on the AVTrack360 dataset show that integrating audio surprise with visual cues reduces bitrate waste by up to 18% compared to visual-only methods.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted at IEEE ICME 2026. 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted manuscript; replaces the v2 withdrawal notice

Multimedia.title: Enhanced image forensics through partial C2PA-based provenance information
Multimedia.summary: Cryptographically verifiable C2PA-based Content Credentials (CCs) can be attached to freshly acquired or generated digital images but also to already existing ones with no previous provenance information, for instance after processing through trusted C2PA-enabled software tools. The latter case leads to images with so-called partial CCs, which capture only the last operations applied, while prior provenance remains unknown and can be investigated through signal forensics. This paper addresses the forensic analysis of such images, highlighting the opportunity to leverage the partial CCs as additional trusted knowledge to adapt forensic detectors towards the statistical characteristics of the image under analysis and mitigate potential distribution shifts. To this end, a two-step strategy is envisioned: (i) reconstructing the operations applied by the last signer through a structural analysis of the partial CCs; (ii) exploiting the obtained reconstruction to enhance the forensic detector of the analyst through an adaptation process. An empirical analysis on partial CCs produced by commercial C2PA-enabled software tools through different editing operations is carried out, providing evidence on the feasibility of the reconstruction in practical cases. An experimental case study on the forensic task of synthetic image detection is then presented, showing that the proposed strategy can significantly enhance the performance of state-of-the-art detectors on test images that are postprocessed via C2PA-enabled software tools after being generated/acquired.
Multimedia.comment: paper accepted to IEEE International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security (WIFS) 2026

Multimedia.title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation
Multimedia.summary: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feature distillation with text and click conditioning, and then fine-tune the separator using the adapted visual features. We also introduce an on-screen interference setting, where both the target and interferer are visible, to evaluate target selectivity. Experiments on standard benchmarks and the on-screen interference setting demonstrate consistent improvements in separation quality and target selectivity, particularly for mixtures containing semantically similar sources.
Multimedia.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027

Multimedia.title: TSM diff: A new Parallel-Tree-Traversal Algorithm for the Comparison of Music Score Files
Multimedia.summary: Music score files are more difficult to compare than their text-based equivalents, as their content is more complex and organised into hierarchical structures. This explains the lack of tools for processing music scores similar to the widely used old Unix diff command. We propose a new algorithm and tool for comparing digital music scores in various encodings, such as MusicXML or MEI, based on a graph-structured abstract representation called Tree Score Model (TSM). Given two scores, after conversion into TSM, our procedure calculates jointly: A list of differences, localised by time positions in the input scores; A time distance, cumulated duration of time-spans where scores differ; An edit distance, called surface distance, based on notational attributes not related to time. The two later measures are normalised and combined into a similarity distance between scores. Our procedure has been implemented in C++ and is available as a Python module. Our first experiments have shown a very good efficiency even on challenging data. As a proof of concept, we propose two demos based on different versions of some Mozart's piano sonata, and transcriptions of monophonic soli on the same jazz standards by different performers. https://tsm-diff-lbd-7a7e2a.gitlab.io/demo.html

Multimedia.title: Influence of Agent Number and Behavior on Users' Psychological Responses in VR Evacuation Training
Multimedia.summary: This study aims to build effective drill software by combining a virtual simulation of a disaster with multiple agents capable of expressing emotions. We evaluated how the number of agents and their emotional and behavioral actions during evacuation influence users in a virtual space. The results showed that users tended to act more confidently when many agents evacuated with them, and that the evacuation route chosen by the agents influenced the users' decision-making. These findings indicate that users' evacuation behavior is shaped not only by the environment itself but also by the collective behavior of surrounding agents, underscoring the need to consider how agent behavior affects users' psychological states during training.
Multimedia.comment: The 2nd International Workshop on Trust and Blame in Multi-Person Multi-Agent Societies (TBSA_2nd) in conjunction with HAI 2026, 7 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables

Multimedia.title: GSVC: Efficient Video Representation and Compression Through 2D Gaussian Splatting
Multimedia.summary: In this work, we explore 2D Gaussian splat as a new primitive for representing and compressing videos, showing its promise as an alternative to traditional signal-based primitives. We introduce GSVC, a new Gaussian splatting-based video codec that incorporates common techniques used in classical video codecs to exploit temporal redundancy between nearby frames. In GSVC, each frame is represented by a set of overlapping Gaussian splats, which, when rendered together, approximate the original frame. Gaussian splats for the first frame and subsequent frames following scene changes (called anchor frames) are learned from scratch, while the remaining frames (called propagation frames) are initialized from the Gaussian splats of their previous frames and then fine-tuned. Scene changes are detected through loss differences during the training process. To capture large motion or newly appeared objects, we randomly add Gaussian splats to propagation frames before fine-tuning. GSVC supports a knob for rate-distortion trade-offs through controlling the number of Gaussian splats for each frame. Gaussian splats with low contributions to the frame quality can be removed during training. GSVC supports two-pass encoding by propagating the Gaussian splats from a future propagation frame back to an anchor frame, further improving the video quality for challenging video scenes. To achieve efficient compression, GSVC uses a residual-based Gaussian splats quantization framework that encodes only changes to the Gaussian parameters between frames. Experimental results show that GSVC achieves rate-distortion performance comparable to state-of-the-art video codec implementations for AV1 and VVC. GSVC inherits the advantages of Gaussian splatting in rendering, allowing it to achieve the rendering speed of 1500 fps for a $1920\times 1080$ video. Project page: https://longanwang-cs.github.io/gsvc/.
Multimedia.comment: 23 pages, 15 figures, 1 table. Extended version of our NOSSDAV 2025 paper

Multimedia.title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
Multimedia.summary: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. It introduces neural audio codecs and autoencoders, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization in a shared notation. Worked examples connect training objectives and sampling procedures to published systems. The application sections relate the musical requirements of instrumental generation, songs, editing, and live performance to model design. Comparison tables record representations, methods, inputs, tasks, and release information documented in papers and official sources. Symbolic composition, speech, and sound effects are included where they connect to music audio. We explain how to interpret automatic metrics and learned judges, design and report listening tests, and assess evidence about data provenance, memorization, attribution, and output detection. Selected legal decisions and disputes illustrate the implications for training and release. The reviewed systems combine established generative paradigms with new representations, planning stages, and post-training procedures. Differences in data, scale, and evaluation limit what cross-system comparisons can establish about the sources of reported gains.

Image and Video Processing.title: AlbumVSR: Identity-Preserving Face Video Super-Resolution from a Personal Photo Album
Image and Video Processing.summary: Severe blur, downsampling, noise, and compression can erase the identity cues needed to faithfully restore a person's face. We therefore use photographs of the same person as an external source of identity. AlbumVSR conditions a frozen, one-step streaming diffusion transformer on a personal album. We use four MagFace/CLIP set tokens to encode the album, and 64 texture tokens which come from a fused UV atlas rendered at the current window's estimated face pose. These tokens are appended to the transformer's cached cross-attention context. On an identity-disjoint VoxCeleb2 benchmark with heavy synthetic degradation, AlbumVSR raises ArcFace similarity to the ground truth from 0.586 to 0.670 and face PSNR from 24.98 to 26.71 dB. On the 91 test identities, its mean identity similarity is higher than that of all 14 baselines.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Nianyao Du and Xijun Wang contributed equally

Image and Video Processing.title: Guidance-Coupled Nullspace Drifting for One-Step Medical Image Reconstruction
Image and Video Processing.summary: Generative reconstruction can recover high-quality images from undersampled acquisitions, but state-of-the-art generative priors commonly rely on iterative sampling. Reducing the number of iterations lowers inference cost but also removes opportunities for progressive distributional refinement, making it difficult to retain image realism without sacrificing reconstruction fidelity. Drift modeling offers an alternative by shifting progressive refinement to training, thereby enabling one-step sampling without an iterative inference trajectory. Existing drifting methods, however, do not account for the imaging operator when modeling distributional drift. We propose DriftRecon, a generative method for one-step medical image reconstruction that performs drifting directly in the nullspace of the imaging operator. DriftRecon uses nullspace-restricted noise to construct training samples and a multiscale generator that incorporates measurement conditioning across resolution levels, with its generated component projected onto the operator nullspace. To control the fidelity--realism trade-off at inference, a conditional guidance parameter continuously steers the same generator between measurement-conditioned and unconditional generation. We derive a guidance-dependent similarity-kernel temperature schedule that preserves the guidance-weighted mass receiving strengthened supervision, thereby progressively localizing drift interactions as guidance increases to limit the associated loss of reconstruction fidelity. Experiments in sparse-view CT and accelerated MRI reconstruction show that DriftRecon outperforms established generative reconstruction methods and recent drifting models while producing reconstructions in a single forward pass.

Image and Video Processing.title: Hardwired Distributed Processing Units at the Sensor: Truly Parallel Vision Pre-Processing that Frees the Host CPU
Image and Video Processing.summary: Conventional vision pipelines route every pixel to a host processor, which must then wait for a complete frame before it can act and devote part of each frame period to routine pre-processing. We examine an alternative organisation in which this work is distributed across hardwired distributed processing units (HDPUs): small, fixed datapaths attached directly to the sensor, each committed to a single always-on task, operating truly in parallel on the same pixel stream and delivering compact results to the host. From one library of 3x3 operators sharing a common two-clock latency, we construct three HDPUs (Canny edges, Harris corners, and a line tracker that issues a steering decision) and run them side by side on a single camera stream in a low-cost Artix-7 FPGA, at a cost of 2,568 LUTs and an estimated 0.318 W. Every stage of every unit is bit-exact with its software model. In a full-system simulation with a datasheet camera model, each decision leaves its HDPU within 11.03 camera lines of the pixel that produced it, 22-67x sooner than the earliest moment at which a frame-based program on the host could respond; the HDPU latency varies by no more than 17 ns, whereas the host's own run times reached 12.5x their median. Offloading the three tasks returns 18-30% of a core to the host in every frame period at 640x480, and 63% of the frame period, with all threads in use, at 1080p. The cost of the units grows with frame width only through their line buffers, and in a closed-loop model of a line-following vehicle the HDPU raises the highest speed at which the line is held from 4.75 to 10.00 m/s.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Companion to arXiv:2610.33107

Image and Video Processing.title: Enhanced image forensics through partial C2PA-based provenance information
Image and Video Processing.summary: Cryptographically verifiable C2PA-based Content Credentials (CCs) can be attached to freshly acquired or generated digital images but also to already existing ones with no previous provenance information, for instance after processing through trusted C2PA-enabled software tools. The latter case leads to images with so-called partial CCs, which capture only the last operations applied, while prior provenance remains unknown and can be investigated through signal forensics. This paper addresses the forensic analysis of such images, highlighting the opportunity to leverage the partial CCs as additional trusted knowledge to adapt forensic detectors towards the statistical characteristics of the image under analysis and mitigate potential distribution shifts. To this end, a two-step strategy is envisioned: (i) reconstructing the operations applied by the last signer through a structural analysis of the partial CCs; (ii) exploiting the obtained reconstruction to enhance the forensic detector of the analyst through an adaptation process. An empirical analysis on partial CCs produced by commercial C2PA-enabled software tools through different editing operations is carried out, providing evidence on the feasibility of the reconstruction in practical cases. An experimental case study on the forensic task of synthetic image detection is then presented, showing that the proposed strategy can significantly enhance the performance of state-of-the-art detectors on test images that are postprocessed via C2PA-enabled software tools after being generated/acquired.
Image and Video Processing.comment: paper accepted to IEEE International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security (WIFS) 2026

Image and Video Processing.title: From the Superderivative to a Relative-Gradient Edge Operator
Image and Video Processing.summary: First-derivative edge detectors such as Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts and Scharr measure absolute grey-level differences. We revisit the log-gradient magnitude, a relative-gradient edge operator, and motivate it by analogy with the superderivative, a multiplicative derivative in which the independent variable is perturbed multiplicatively rather than additively. In one and two dimensions the logarithm of the superderivative is a radial logarithmic derivative; its local, origin-free, isotropic analogue is the magnitude of the logarithmic gradient. The resulting operator measures relative rather than absolute change, giving an edge-strength map that is invariant under global intensity rescaling. We present the theory, show how the operator can be implemented in two steps---a classical gradient kernel plus a pointwise division---and compare it with standard first-derivative filters on synthetic images with ground-truth edges and on the official BSDS500 benchmark. We also study a parametric family that interpolates between the absolute gradient and the log-gradient; empirically, the best members are small intermediate exponents, which edge the classical kernels by a small but statistically detectable margin in the per-image metric and, with the same Gaussian smoothing as the single-$σ$ Canny, match it in ODS and lead it in OIS and AP, while the tuned Canny remains ahead in ODS. The single-threshold margin over the kernels does not replicate on the held-out test split, and the fully relative endpoint is never the best member, its ranking depending on the edge-map normalisation. The contribution is the construction and the invariance it buys, not a new state of the art.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 15 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer
Image and Video Processing.summary: Can a Watershed transform, the classical tool of morphological segmentation, be placed at the end of a deep network and trained through? The Power Watershed (PW) is the limit of the seeded Random Walker (RW) as p grows to infinity with edge weights raised to the power p. At every finite p the RW solves a sparse positive-definite linear system and is exactly differentiable with respect to the edge weights and the unaries through one adjoint solve; its multi-label form costs one right-hand side per label, and its limit is the PW. We study this family as the last layer of a segmentation network, the watershed layer (WS layer). A conditioning study measures how the solve, the gradient and the distance to the limit evolve with p, and the implicit gradient is checked against unrolling. On synthetic data with correct edge costs the WS layer transforms a soft prediction into an exact boundary. On nuclei segmentation (PanNuke), a binary WS layer is level with a thresholded U-Net. With the instances as labels, the WS layer turns the U-Net into an instance segmenter whose number of labels is set per image by the markers rather than by the output layout, and the network is trained through that partition: instance F1 score rises from 0.656 to 0.795 over a U-Net with connected components, level with the same network followed by a tuned marker watershed. At the training temperature the partition is a watershed of the learned costs, and the finite temperature lets the solve hedge, discounting weak markers and sharing contested pixels. The hedging puts the WS layer 0.015--0.020 F1 ahead of the baseline when trained on a tenth of the data, at the price of having to deploy the finite-p solve rather than its exact limit at inference. Code and the full experimental record are released.

Image and Video Processing.title: Morphological Decoupling-Based Skeletal Classification for Clinical Assessment of Malocclusion
Image and Video Processing.summary: Malocclusion skeletal grading is a fundamental task in orthodontics, critical for diagnosis and treatment planning. Traditionally, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is used for visual measurement, and the reconstructed lateral cephalograms are handed over to expert dentists for diagnosis. However, manual review is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and subject to inter-operator variability. Therefore, an automatic CBCT-based system is needed for reliable malocclusion skeletal grading. In this case, we develop TeethGNN, a novel graph-based framework designed to combine CBCT image features with morphological information for accurate and efficient malocclusion grading. TeethGNN utilizes a decoupled learnable decoder to directly predict key morphological indicators from CBCT images, eliminating the need for manual measurements. These morphological features are then fused with image features using a graph neural network (GNN), which effectively models the relationships between the modalities. To further enhance robustness and calibration, we introduce a collaborative calibration strategy. This strategy combines multi-scale graph adversarial perturbation for explicit calibration and nonlinear topological graph calibration for implicit confidence adjustment. Extensive experiments and ablation studies on our collected clinical dataset demonstrate that our malocclusion measurement system achieves 77.08\% in accuracy and 89.61\% in AUC, outperforming the compared state-of-the-art methods. These results validate the effectiveness of graph-based multimodal fusion and collaborative calibration in improving malocclusion grading performance. Our system shows strong potential for advancing computer-aided orthodontic diagnosis, providing an accurate and reliable solution for vision-based clinical measurement and diagnosis.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted by Biocybernetics and Biomedical Engineering

Image and Video Processing.title: CylindTrack: Depth-Aware Cylindrical Motion Modeling for Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking in Mobile Robots
Image and Video Processing.summary: Maintaining consistent target identities and observation histories is essential for mobile robot perception. Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) benefits from broad visual coverage but must address coordinate discontinuities at the equirectangular image seam and fluctuations in relative-depth estimates. Such fluctuations can undermine depth-aware association, highlighting the need for temporally consistent depth cues. We propose CylindTrack, a depth-aware cylindrical tracking-by-detection framework that jointly models panoramic topology and temporal depth consistency. Depth-Temporal Trajectory Modeling (DTM) maintains instance depth and its rate of change as filtered trajectory states. Spherical Spatio-Temporal Consistency Learning (SSTC) combines a Temporal Mixer with Spherical Geometry-aware Attention to refine depth-aware representations. A Topology-Aware Cylindrical Motion Model (TCMM) represents horizontal motion in an unwrapped angular state and incorporates periodic overlap, angular consistency, and filtered depth cues into association. Experiments on QuadTrack and JRDB demonstrate improved identity consistency and trajectory continuity, with HOTA scores of 33.67 and 31.12 and IDF1 scores of 40.45 and 34.33, respectively. The framework processes 28.56 and 21.34 frames per second, respectively, on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU under the reported evaluation settings. These results support persistent panoramic multi-object tracking for mobile robot perception. The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack.
Image and Video Processing.comment: The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack

Image and Video Processing.title: What Does LOL Measure? Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks
Image and Video Processing.summary: LOL-v1 and LOLv2-Real are the standard benchmarks for supervised low-light image enhancement, and several leading methods ship hand-set test-time adjustments with their evaluation scripts. We audit both benchmarks with 18 public checkpoints of eight methods under one metric implementation that reproduces every published number to within 0.09 dB, and find that their test labels differ from their training labels. (i) The 15 LOL-v1 test labels are rendered differently: the same captures appear in LOLv2 with labels of identical luminance but 1.48x lower saturation, and LOL-v1's own training labels match the LOLv2 rendering; we confirm this on the official release. (ii) The LOLv2-Real test set is the contiguous block of images 690-789, whose labels are 14% darker than the training labels (Cliff's delta = -0.45, p < 1e-12) with no comparable shift in the input statistics we examined; methods trained without any labels score up to 5.5 dB higher on test than on train. (iii) All 15 LOL-v1 test inputs reappear in LOLv2-Real, 12 in its training set. The released test-time settings are consistent with compensating for these shifts. Separating what can be calibrated on training data from what only test-set tuning finds, the test-only residual has median 0.00 dB on LOLv2-Syn, which has no shift, but 0.37 dB on LOL-v1 and 0.92 dB on LOLv2-Real (up to 3.9 dB). Under the shift, test-set checkpoint selection inflates a from-scratch model by 0.9-2.0 dB, and removing the released settings changes which method ranks first. We give concrete reporting recommendations.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: Cross-Device Transfer of a Hospital-Trained Fetal Head Circumference Model to a Low-Cost Handheld Ultrasound Probe
Image and Video Processing.summary: Automated fetal head circumference (HC) measurement reaches near-expert accuracy on the HC18 benchmark, but published models are trained and evaluated on hospital-grade equipment. We quantify what happens when such a model is carried to a low-cost handheld probe. A lightweight segmentation network (CSM, 0.13M parameters) was trained on HC18 across five independent runs and applied without modification to images from a $1,350 handheld probe (SonoQue C3), acquired at the same visit as the reference hospital scan in 18 patients. In-domain accuracy was 2.34 +/- 0.43 mm; on handheld images the same model gave 16.12 mm against the hospital record, a 6.9-fold degradation. Input preprocessing, a choice rarely reported, accounted for about a third of that gap: direct resizing gave 49.45 mm against 16.12 mm for an aspect-preserving pipeline. A leave-one-out data-efficiency curve showed that fine-tuning on two images significantly worsened accuracy, and that from four images upward error fell by 0.75 mm per doubling of the local dataset (p = 0.0045), although no training-set size up to 27 images significantly improved on the unmodified model. Much of the residual gap belongs to the reference rather than the model: scored against a manual tracing of the same image the model was already within 10.48 mm, and its disagreement with sonographer calipers on the same frame was a near-constant offset, negative in 10 of 10 cases. A single calibration constant estimated leave-one-out reduced that disagreement from 8.12 mm to 3.49 mm, reaching the intraobserver reproducibility reported for experienced sonographers, but did not improve agreement with the hospital record. Cross-device evaluations should therefore report the input preprocessing used and characterise the precision of their reference standard.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 24 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: Report-Derived Labels, an Image Teacher and the Gap to Expert Labels in Knee MRI: An Analysis of One Entry to the RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection Challenge
Image and Video Processing.summary: In the RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection challenge, 58 of 4,407 training studies have expert labels for 12 findings, and the rest have only a radiology report. We compare training targets built from a language-model reading of the reports and from a public image model against two references: the expert labels and the 39,248 study-finding cells that the reports state as present or absent. The report labels and the out-of-fold predictions of the image model reach similar agreement with the expert labels (macro AUC 0.892 and 0.896) but fail on different findings. The report is better for ligament tears and patellofemoral osteoarthritis, which it never calls present when the experts do not; the image model is better for effusion, Baker's cyst, contusion, and synovitis, where the reports call the finding absent, leave it out, or call it present more often than the experts. Their equal mixture reaches 0.927 (gain over the report labels 0.035, 95% interval 0.019 to 0.052), also after removing the studies whose knee side was handled inconsistently. We did not observe a model-level gain from this better target: a 2.5D ResNet50 trained on the report labels alone scored 0.877 on the private leaderboard, after the deadline, against 0.872 for the same model trained on the mixture, and the out-of-fold advantage of the mixture is confounded by a change of code and by possible leakage through the image model's folds. A scanner prevalence prior raised agreement with the reports but not with the experts, so a report-derived reference can reward reporting habits. A rank correction for co-occurring findings gave small out-of-fold gains and no visible leaderboard effect. Our entry, a forked public ensemble with that correction, was displayed at rank 582 of 6,299 on the private leaderboard (0.943, a score shared by 287 teams). All results are exploratory; none of the models is meant for clinical use.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 24 pages, 10 figures, 14 tables. Code: https://github.com/soheilkooklan/rsna-knee-report-labels

Image and Video Processing.title: TheseusSyn: Unified Medical Image Synthesis via Context-Conditioned Masked Autoregression
Image and Video Processing.summary: High-fidelity medical image synthesis is promising for data-efficient learning and privacy-preserving model development. However, most existing approaches rely on symbolic or label-based conditioning, which constrains generative diversity and limits case-specific contextual fidelity. Inspired by the Ship of Theseus paradox, we propose TheseusSyn, a novel context-conditioned synthesis paradigm that generates images through iterative content replacement. Our framework employs a multi-codebook discrete tokenizer to convert medical images into sequences of token indices, extracted with a global representation token that serves as a contextual constraint. A masked autoregressive generative model then iteratively masks and predicts tokens conditioned on both local neighborhoods and the global context. By progressively replacing image content until the entire token sequence is renewed, TheseusSyn produces synthetic samples that preserve anatomical coherence and semantic consistency while introducing controlled diversity. We evaluate the proposed framework on multiple datasets from MedMNIST by constructing synthetic datasets with varying masking strategies and training ResNet-18 classifiers exclusively on either real or synthetic data. Experimental results demonstrate that classifiers trained on TheseusSyn-generated images achieve competitive performance on official test sets, indicating that the synthesized data preserve diagnostically relevant features and semantic consistency. Systematic analysis of masking strategies reveals their impact on structural fidelity and downstream classification accuracy. These results suggest that context-conditioned masked autoregression provides an effective and generalizable solution for label-free medical image synthesis, offering a scalable alternative to conventional data augmentation and class-conditioned generative models in medical imaging applications.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures

Image and Video Processing.title: DiffUltra: Task-Guided Pathology Synthesis for Large-Scale Real-World Lung Ultrasound Data
Image and Video Processing.summary: Despite their scale, large medical imaging datasets may underrepresent clinically relevant pathological presentations. Synthetic data can expand coverage, but findings must remain compatible with surrounding anatomy. This is challenging in ultrasound, where findings resemble surrounding tissue and must be positioned relative to anatomical landmarks. We propose DiffUltra, a task-guided latent diffusion pipeline that models pathological structure and spatial context, and screens synthetic images for downstream utility. DiffUltra conditions generation on structural masks decomposing findings into anechoic, hypoechoic, and hyperechoic subregions. Two placement strategies insert findings into pathology-absent backgrounds or replace existing findings with structurally matched pathology from other patients. A filter trained exclusively on real data retains images whose predictions agree spatially with target boxes. We evaluate DiffUltra for lung ultrasound detection of pleural effusion and consolidation, using over 700,000 expert-annotated frames from 598 patients at 12 sites. Averaged across three real-data scales, synthetic insertion significantly improved video-level AUROC for both pleural effusion (p = 0.017) and consolidation (p < 0.01). For pleural effusion, frame-level average precision improved by 4.5 percentage points on average and by 6.1 points using only 10% of real data (p < 0.01 for both). Synthetic insertion also yielded larger average precision gains than an existing diffusion-based lesion-insertion method at every scale. At full scale, targeted synthesis improved AUROC for both pathologies by 1.1-3.9 points in an underrepresented anatomical zone and on a held-out acquisition system. These results suggest that anatomically constrained, task-guided synthesis can help address coverage gaps in ultrasound training data.
Image and Video Processing.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Image and Video Processing.title: Anchored Fusion for Automated Airway Segmentation in Pediatric and Adult CT
Image and Video Processing.summary: Airway segmentation from chest CT enables branch-level measurement of airway size and growth, but peripheral bronchi remain hard to segment, particularly in children, whose airways are smaller and for whom few annotated scans exist. Different models recover complementary branches of the airway tree. Their union improves overall tree coverage but also introduces disconnected non-airway objects. We propose anchored fusion (A-Fuse), which takes the voxel-wise union of TfeNet, a retrained MEDPSeg and a reimplemented AirMorph and retains the connected component with greatest overlap with the AirMorph mask. On 30 held-out adult CTs from the ATM'26 training set, A-Fuse reaches a Dice score of 93.24% and the highest branch detection rate among compared methods (92.05%). On nine pediatric scans, it reaches 94.15% Dice and 68.79% branch detection. A-Fuse retains the airway tree in all 39 test scans, whereas keeping the largest component selects a non-airway object in four. A-Fuse is deployed as an automated web application and we release all code, trained weights and an open-source ITK-SNAP extension for 3D tubular segmentation editing.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Code, weights and web application: https://github.com/quin-med-harvard-edu/airway-seg

Image and Video Processing.title: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
Image and Video Processing.summary: Most deep learning systems for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are evaluated on a single data source, with limited evidence of cross-site generalisation, uncertainty calibration, and interpretability. We propose CalibCause, a quality-gated mixture-of-experts framework that combines per-expert visual explanations, label-free image-quality conditioning, knowledge distillation, and calibrated confidence with deferral. We evaluated the framework using 51,310 fundus images from EyePACS, DDR, and APTOS 2019, with IDRiD and DeepDRiD for external testing. Evaluation included pooled testing, leave-one-environment-out experiments, paired bootstrap confidence intervals, and local grade-threshold adaptation. On the pooled test split, the label-free distilled student achieved quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863 and accuracy of 0.865 with 27.8 million parameters, 52% fewer than its teacher. Across held-out environments, the label-free model achieved mean QWK of 0.741 compared with 0.743 for a plain ConvNeXt-Tiny baseline, while adversarial invariance did not improve cross-site grading accuracy. Refitting grade thresholds using 200 labelled images increased held-out EyePACS QWK from 0.533 to 0.621 for the label-free model. After vector scaling, expected calibration error ranged from 0.025 to 0.036 across CalibCause variants, and deferring the least confident 20% of images increased student accuracy from 0.865 to 0.923 on the remaining images. These findings demonstrate that quality-aware grading, interpretable expert routing, model compression, and calibrated deferral can be integrated without sacrificing cross-site performance relative to a plain baseline, although reliable deployment still requires local validation and adaptation.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: Optimal Sampling and Noise Mitigation for Vocal Fold Kinematics in High-Speed Videoendoscopy
Image and Video Processing.summary: Objectives: High-Speed Videoendoscopy glottal area waveforms conflate lateral fold excursion with longitudinal opening, precluding direct estimation of velocity, acceleration, and left-right asymmetry. Displacement waveforms preserve these quantities but are susceptible to spatial quantization and temporal sampling errors. We characterize these errors, evaluate reduction via Kalman smoothing and temporal interpolation, and determine optimal frame rate bounds relative to pixel excursion, speed quotient (SQ), and open quotient (OQ). Methods: Sampling theory was used to derive analytical frame-rate bounds required for kinematic feature fidelity. Kalman smoothing was compared with FFT-based denoising, paired with sinc or spline interpolation. Interpolation was evaluated on 4000 fps recordings (N=55) downsampled and reconstructed. A 16000 fps dataset (N=12) served as reference for noise reduction across 2000-8000 fps downsampled waveforms evaluated on peak displacement, velocity, OQ, and SQ. Results: Sinc interpolation yielded lower median mean absolute error than spline (0.29 vs 0.52 pixels), with 85% of recordings (47/55) versus 45% (25/55) below 0.5 pixels. For kinematic feature estimation (N=12), Kalman-sinc outperformed FFT-sinc in 75% of feature-by-frame-rate pairings. Conclusion: Computing kinematic features without artifacts requires joint consideration of temporal and spatial resolution. Kalman-sinc preprocessing at 8000 fps is recommended for velocity and SQ measures. Peak lateral displacement can be measured at 2000 fps, while OQ requires 4000 fps for typical spatial resolutions (9-14 pixels maximum excursion). Pixel excursion should be reported alongside kinematic measures to contextualize data reliability.
Image and Video Processing.comment: This is the preprint Auhors manuscript to be published in Journal of Voice

Systems and Control.title: Tunable Spatial Task Allocation with Application to Maritime Swarms
Systems and Control.summary: In this chapter, we explore how a team of autonomous agents can flexibly reconfigure the distribution of its members across many spatially embedded tasks using a task allocation strategy grounded in a generalization of the recently proposed Nonlinear Opinion Dynamics model. Motivated by an adaptive maritime survey application, we couple opinion dynamics directly to spatial movement and examine how the emergent macroscopic allocation is shaped by the interplay between environmental geometry, nature of social interactions, and task demands. We illustrate in simulation how social coupling in the model tunes group cohesion, producing macroscopic allocation patterns ranging from maximally dispersed states, to intermediate semi-dispersed states with a smaller number of distinct subgroups, to maximally cohesive consensus states, in distinct and interpretable parameter regimes. Furthermore, we demonstrate with illustrative examples how a team can reconfigure itself in real time under changing task demands. For allocation scenarios with distance-based task preference and matched number of agents and tasks, we relate numerically the final allocation in the group to the Hungarian optimum, illustrating close-to-optimal performance. We illustrate performance of this method under realistic communication constraints in the MOOS-IvP-Multi simulation environment with simulated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Together, these examples show how a common set of local interaction rules can support a large range of interpretable macroscopic allocation states and flexible transitions between them.

Systems and Control.title: A Spectral Perspective on Stochastic Control Barrier Functions
Systems and Control.summary: Stochastic control barrier functions (SCBFs) provide a safety-critical control framework for systems subject to stochastic disturbances by bounding the probability of remaining within a safe set. However, finding a valid SCBF that explicitly reflects the long-horizon behavior of the true safety probability remains a challenge. This paper addresses this issue by adopting a spectral perspective, utilizing the linear operator that governs the evolution of the closed-loop system's safety probability. We find that the dominant eigenpair of this Koopman-like operator encodes fundamental safety information of the stochastic system. The dominant eigenfunction is a natural and valid SCBF, with values that characterize relative asymptotic safety across initial states, while the dominant eigenvalue indicates the global asymptotic rate at which the safety probability decays. A practical algorithm for computation is proposed, termed power-policy iteration, which jointly estimates the dominant eigenpair while updating the backup policy with the aim of improving long-term safety. The method is validated using simulation experiments on safety-critical dynamics models.
Systems and Control.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

Systems and Control.title: Activate the Dual Cones: A Tight Reformulation of Conic ACOPF Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: By exploiting the observed tightness of dual rotated second-order cone (RSOC) constraints, this paper transforms the dual of a conic ACOPF relaxation into an equivalent, non-conic problem where dual constraints are implicitly enforced through eliminated dual RSOC variables. To accomplish this, we apply the RSOC-based Jabr relaxation of ACOPF, pose its dual, and then show that all dual RSOC constraints must be tight (i.e., active) at optimality. We then construct a reduced dual maximization problem with only non-negativity constraints, avoiding the explicit RSOC inequality constraints. Numerical experiments confirm that the tight formulation recovers the same dual objective values as a mature conic solver (e.g., MOSEK via PowerModels) on various PGLib benchmark test systems (ranging from 3- to 1354-buses). The proposed formulation has useful performance benefits, compared with its conic counterpart, and it allows us to define a bounding function which provides a guaranteed lower bound on system cost. While this paper focuses on demonstrating the correctness and validity of the proposed structural simplification, it lays the groundwork for future GPU-accelerated first-order optimization methods which can exploit the unconstrained nature of the proposed formulation.

Systems and Control.title: Selective Sliding Mode Control Enhances Robustness of Aerial Robots Under Disturbances
Systems and Control.summary: Quadrotor control under disturbances such as wind gusts and payload variations remains challenging. First-order sliding mode control (SMC) and matched/unmatched uncertainty distinction are classical approaches; however, neither tells a practitioner which loops in a cascaded controller should be made robust to sustain disturbances, how to tune those loops, nor what the additional costs are on an embedded processor. Applying robust control uniformly across all axes addresses disturbances indiscriminately, adding tuning effort on axes where no disturbance acts. On inherently underactuated vehicles, disturbances along some axes cannot be opposed directly at all. We propose a principled methodology for deciding where robust control belongs in a cascaded architecture, with all control running onboard the vehicle. We recover the acting disturbance from PID hover flights under disturbance by inverting the equations of motion, use the recovered signal to identify and quantify the excited axes, and deploy robust control where it counts. Experiments on a Crazyflie 2.1 quadrotor under slung-payload and oblique-wind disturbances show tracking improvements concentrated on the axes the rule selects, and gain sweeps confirm that the switching gain reduces error on matched axes but has no effect on an excited unmatched axis, as the analysis predicts.

Systems and Control.title: Stability and Controllability Margins of Water Network Hydraulics
Systems and Control.summary: Pump and valve actuation in water distribution networks (WDNs) affects how pressures, flows, and tank levels respond to demand changes and other disturbances. This paper presents a stability and controllability analysis of WDN hydraulics. Starting from a general nonlinear differential algebraic equation (DAE) model of WDNs with arbitrary topology and network components (valves and pumps), we investigate three questions. First, we study local well-posedness of the network dynamics and characterize the loss of differentiability introduced by pump and valve switching. Second, we introduce regularization methods that smooth flow and pressure trajectories under changing controls. Third, we quantify how network parametric uncertainty impacts local stability and controllability, while establishing error bounds on the resulting margins. For water operations, stability means that pressures and flows return to steady values after a disturbance, and controllability means that pump and valve actions can move pressures, flows, and tank levels; the margins we compute measure how far a network is from losing either. We demonstrate that the proposed DAE models produce trajectories that closely match EPANET, a widely used WDN simulator, for benchmark networks. The case studies also show that the WDN DAE relates the recovery of pressures and flows to a weighted Laplacian of the network, ranks pipes by their effect on the local dynamics, and reveals that certain demand variation changes the stability and controllability margins without eliminating local stability or the ability of pumps to affect pressures and flows. The developed theoretical foundations enable network analysis, mitigation strategies, and system design.

Systems and Control.title: Inertial Steering and Motion Prediction of Tracked Vehicles on Low-Adherence Surfaces
Systems and Control.summary: Tracked vehicles are widely used in off-road applications, but their conventional motion models often rely on no-slip assumptions that become inaccurate on low-adherence surfaces. Rather than treating inertial effects arising from slip as a disturbance to be minimized, this work investigates how inertial effects arising from a moving mass can be deliberately exploited for steering on low-friction surfaces. A dynamic model for an articulated tracked vehicle with a passive trailer is developed, allowing inertial effects from trailer motion to be captured. The approach is experimentally evaluated on ice, where our dynamic model outperforms the kinematic baseline. We also propose a mixed dynamic-kinematic model to adapt predictions to both surface and situation by exploiting predictions from both methods. Finally, we demonstrate inertial steering on a mono-track vehicle without a conventional steering mechanism, showing that controlled movements of an internal mass can generate turning motion on ice. The resulting behavior can be predicted using the proposed dynamic model by representing the internal mass as a frictionless trailer, revealing the analogous dynamics between the two configurations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of inertial steering as an alternative steering mechanism for tracked vehicles operating in low-adherence environments.

Systems and Control.title: Efficient MPC for LC-Filtered Three-Level NPC Inverters in Vehicle-to-Load Applications
Systems and Control.summary: Finite control-set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) offers fast, modulator-free voltage regulation but is sensitive to the fidelity of its internal model. This sensitivity is usually countered by algorithmic augmentation, disturbance observers, adaptive weighting, or learning-based estimators, at the cost of extra tuning and computation. This paper instead improves fidelity at the source. For a three-level neutral-point-clamped (3L-NPC) inverter with an LC output filter in vehicle-to-load operation, a coupled alpha-beta-frame predictive model carries the capacitor voltage and filter current jointly through the state vector, so that the second-order LC coupling is retained without enlarging the 27-candidate search. The cost function additionally regulates dc-link neutral-point balance and switching effort. One-step prediction accuracy, parametric sensitivity, and computational cost are bounded in closed form. Simulation of a V2L system yields a voltage total harmonic distortion of 0.72%, a steady-state tracking error of 1.6%, and transient recovery within one fundamental cycle, meeting the applicable IEEE power-quality limits with margin, without observers, parameter estimation, or learning-based augmentation.

Systems and Control.title: Computationally Constrained First-Order Prediction-Correction Approach for Time-Varying Convex Optimization
Systems and Control.summary: Time-varying optimization methods often predict the locations of time-varying optima, then sample the objective function being minimized, and then compute corrections to those predictions. However, those works typically do not account for settings in which computations are limited. Therefore, in this work we formulate a prediction-correction algorithm that is designed to obey constraints on the total number of iterations it can execute over a given time horizon. We first show that there is a critical threshold for the average number of computations that can be executed between samples of the objective. Then, we show that if the number of allowable computations is above this threshold, then the distance to a time-varying optimum bound decays geometrically. Next, we show that if the number of allowable computations is below that threshold, then the distance to a time-varying optimum still remains bounded. Therefore, it is still possible to track time-varying optima with bounded error even under restrictive limits on the number of computations that can be executed. We also present an algorithm to determine how many prediction and correction steps should be executed for each sample of the objective. Simulation results show that under typical conditions our approach reduces cumulative tracking error by 45.5% compared to a comparable baseline approach.
Systems and Control.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, for submission to ECC

Systems and Control.title: From Local to Global: Sheaf-Theoretic Control Barrier Functions on Manifolds
Systems and Control.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for dynamical systems by rendering a safe set forward-invariant via pointwise-optimal feedback control. While the CBF framework is well established for dynamical systems in Euclidean space, there exist gaps for systems evolving on non-Euclidean manifolds. For systems modeled as constrained control differential inclusions, we introduce the Sheaf-CBF: a sheaf-theoretic framework for CBFs on smooth manifolds and vector bundles. The differential inclusions are formulated intrinsically on the control bundle, and analogous regularity properties in the Euclidean case are established fiberwise under local trivializations. Regularity conditions are given under which a pointwise-optimal feedback law is single-valued and continuous over local charts. Framed as a local-to-global optimization problem, sheaf-theoretic restriction and gluing compatibility conditions on overlapping charts are shown to uniquely determine a continuous global section of the control bundle, thereby guaranteeing forward invariance of the safe set. Numerical simulations on a nontrivial M{ö}bius strip demonstrate that failure of sheaf compatibility results in violations of safety, whereas the Sheaf-CBF maintains forward invariance.

Systems and Control.title: Minimum-Time Trajectory for Escort-Assisted Evasion from a Sensing-Limited Pursuer
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies a minimum-time path-planning problem in which an escort assists a leader by triggering and redirecting a sensing-limited pursuer. For the post-engagement case with equal leader, escort, and pursuer speeds, we show that the minimum-time leader trajectory has a three-phase structure: an initial straight segment, a moving-boundary segment, and a final straight segment to the goal. The boundary-following kinematics and the corresponding entry and exit conditions are derived and used to construct the leader trajectory for a fixed escort engagement direction. The engagement direction is then optimized over the feasible set to obtain the minimum-time solution. Numerical results illustrate the resulting trajectory and the benefits of escort assistance.

Systems and Control.title: Finite-Sample Analysis of Model-free Policy Gradient Methods for LQR with Stochastic Data
Systems and Control.summary: Policy gradient (PG) methods are the backbone of many reinforcement learning algorithms due to their good performance in policy optimization problems. As a gradient-based approach, PG methods typically rely on knowledge of the system dynamics. If this is not available, trajectory data can be utilized to approximate first-order information. When the data are noisy, gradient estimates become inaccurate and a study that investigates uncertainty estimation and the analysis of its propagation through the algorithm is currently missing. To address this, our work focuses on the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) problem for systems subject to additive stochastic noise. After briefly summarizing the state of the art for cases with a known model, we focus on scenarios where the system dynamics are unknown, and approximate gradient information is obtained using zeroth-order optimization techniques. We analyze the theoretical properties by computing the error in the estimated gradient and examining how this error affects the convergence of PG algorithms. \textcolor{black}{Additionally, we provide global convergence guarantees for various versions of PG methods, including those employing adaptive step sizes and variance reduction techniques.} This study contributes to characterizing the robustness of model-free PG methods, aiming to identify their limitations in the presence of stochastic noise and proposing improvements to enhance their applicability.

Systems and Control.title: Benchmarking Learning-Based Formula 1 Race Strategies
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents two complementary frameworks to optimize Formula 1 race strategies, jointly accounting for energy allocation, tire wear and pit stop timing. First, the race scenario is modeled using lap time maps and a dynamic tire wear model capturing the main trade-offs arising during a race. Then, we solve the problem by means of a mixed-integer nonlinear program that handles the integer nature of the pit stop decisions. The same race scenario is embedded into a reinforcement learning environment, on which an agent is trained. Providing fast inference at runtime, this method is suited to improve human decision-making during real races. The learned policy's suboptimality is assessed with respect to the optimal solution, both in a nominal scenario and with an unforeseen disturbance. In both cases, the agent achieves approximately 5s of suboptimality on 1.5h of race time, mainly attributable to the different energy allocation strategy. This work lays the foundations for learning-based race strategies and provides a benchmark for future developments.

Systems and Control.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and the noise emission directivity. This leads to over-conservative policies and unexploited wind power. Yet, turbine yaw can simultaneously affect wake interactions and the direction of noise emission, offering an additional degree of freedom for farm-level noise control. We therefore propose Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximise farm power while satisfying a local noise constraint in a defined region. To enable training at a reduced computational cost, a low-fidelity acoustic model is coupled with the steady-state FLORIS simulator. The RL agent effectively learns how to redirect wakes and noise directivity away from the protected region while redistributing power across the farm. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfies the 40 dB noise constraint throughout the full range of turbulent winds, with an average power deficit of only 2% relative to greedy unimpeded control, and up to 7.7% at high wind speeds. In comparison, the industry-standard noise-reduced operation (NRO) baseline here generates an average power loss of 17%. When deployed in the higher-fidelity FASTFarm simulator, the policy largely retains its performance under steady and turbulent inflow, despite differences in simulation fidelity. These results demonstrate the potential of combining yaw control and power derating through RL to improve the power-noise trade-off in wind farm operation.

Systems and Control.title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
Systems and Control.summary: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

Systems and Control.title: Weak and Strong Data Informativity with Structural Priors for System Analysis
Systems and Control.summary: When measurement data are insufficient for unique system identification, data informativity evaluates whether a dataset determines a property across all systems consistent with the data. This paper introduces a unified framework distinguishing between weak and strong data informativity under prior structural knowledge described by affine constraints: data are weakly informative if at least one system consistent with the data and prior knowledge possesses the target property, and strongly informative if every consistent system satisfies it. The latter is consistent with the notion of data informativity in the existing literature. By explicitly parameterizing all consistent systems as affine functions of free parameters via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we characterize these notions for fundamental system properties-including controllability, stabilizability, and stability. This formulation establishes that verifying weak and strong informativity, when tractable, reduces to rank tests of matrix pencils constructed from the data and prior knowledge. Our findings show that structural priors can lower data-excitation requirements and enable reliable analysis even when data fail to be strongly informative. Finally, the framework is extended to a class of noisy data.

Systems and Control.title: Phase-Compensated Frequency-Scan Measurement of Harmonic Transfer Function Impedance
Systems and Control.summary: Impedance models obtained through frequency scanning provides terminal characterization for small-signal stability analysis without requiring detailed knowledge of internal converter parameters. When unbalanced steady-state components introduce cross-frequency coupling, conventional $2\times2$ impedance scan methods must be extended to identify harmonic transfer function (HTF) impedance. However, the measured phases of frequency-coupling terms depend on the starting time of the fast Fourier transform (FFT) window, potentially introducing phase errors when different time references are used. This paper presents a $dq$-domain measurement method of HTF impedance that explicitly accounts for this time dependence. Phase compensation aligns the measured Fourier coefficients to a common electrical phase reference, correcting the resulting phase discrepancies and enabling consistent impedance reconstruction. Comparisons with analytical models under balanced and unbalanced conditions verify the measurement method, recovering the conventional $2\times2$ impedance and the dominant coupling blocks of a $6\times6$ HTF representation, respectively.

Systems and Control.title: A Linear Parameter-Varying Framework for the Analysis of Time-Varying Optimization Algorithms
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper we propose a framework to analyze iterative first-order optimization algorithms for time-varying convex optimization. We assume that the temporal variability is caused by a time-varying parameter entering the objective, which can be measured at the time of decision but whose future values are unknown. We consider the case of strongly convex objective functions with Lipschitz continuous gradients under a convex constraint set. We model the algorithms as discrete-time linear parameter varying (LPV) systems in feedback with monotone operators such as the time-varying gradient. We leverage the approach of analyzing algorithms as uncertain control interconnections with integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) and generalize that framework to the time-varying case. We propose novel IQCs that are capable of capturing the behavior of time-varying nonlinearities and leverage techniques from the LPV literature to establish novel bounds on the tracking error. Quantitative bounds can be computed by solving a semi-definite program and can be interpreted as an input-to-state stability result with respect to a disturbance signal which increases with the temporal variability of the problem. As a departure from results in this research area, our bounds introduce a dependence on different additional measures of temporal variations, such as the function value and gradient rate of change. We exemplify our main results with numerical experiments that showcase how our analysis framework is able to capture convergence rates of different first-order algorithms for time-varying optimization through the choice of IQC and rate bounds.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven Safe Output Regulation of Strict-Feedback Linear Systems with Input Delay
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops a data-driven safe control framework for linear systems possessing a known strict-feedback structure, but with most plant parameters, external disturbances, and input delay being unknown. By leveraging Koopman operator theory, we utilize Krylov dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to extract the system dynamics from measured data, enabling the reconstruction of the system and disturbance matrices. Concurrently, the batch least-squares identification (BaLSI) method is employed to identify other unknown parameters in the input channel. Using control barrier functions (CBFs) and backstepping, we first develop a full-state safe controller. Based on this, we build an output-feedback controller by performing system identification using only the output data and actuation signals as well as constructing an observer to estimate the unmeasured plant states. The proposed approach achieves: 1) finite-time identification of a substantial set of unknown system quantities, and 2) exponential convergence of the output state (the state furthest from the control input) to a reference trajectory while rigorously ensuring safety constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a safe vehicle platooning application.

Systems and Control.title: Whittle Index Policy for Three State Collapsing Bandits
Systems and Control.summary:
Partially observable restless multi-armed bandit models have been studied for dynamic resource allocation problems under uncertainty. This paper analyzes three-state restless multi-armed bandits with partial observability. These are called collapsing bandit problems if the state of an arm (bandit) is perfectly observable when it is scheduled for allocation. The state is not observable when the arm is not scheduled. The planner has a budget constraint on the scheduling decisions in each time slot. The planner's goal is to maximize expected cumulative long term discounted reward. We study the Whittle index policy. To analyze index policy, first the $N$-armed collapsing bandit problem is decoupled into $N$ single arm problems, and convexity and monotonicity of the optimal value function in belief vector are derived using monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) ordering on state transition dynamics and monotone reward structure assumption.
  We next show that the optimal policy is of threshold type in belief under sufficiency conditions on the model. These sufficiency conditions depend on Lipschitz bound on the value function in the belief. We further prove the indexability for an arm using Lipschitz bound on subsidy sensitivity with minimal restrictive assumption on the transition probability model and discount factor $β.$ Our results generalize to three state and strengthen existing results on threshold policy and indexability with weaker model assumptions. We provide index computation algorithm and we present comparison of the Whittle-index, myopic policy and round-robin policies in the simulation study.

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Orbit-Aided Vector Tracking for Orbit Determination of LEO Satellites
Systems and Control.summary: Reliable orbit determination for CubeSats is essential for emerging low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation, and timing (LEO-PNT) applications. However, onboard orbit determination remains constrained by single-frequency GNSS code-based receivers, intermittent signal reception, and highly dynamic orbital conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive orbit-aided vector tracking (OAVT) algorithm for LEO-PNT CubeSat orbit determination under these conditions. The method employs a GNSS vector tracking loop (VTL) as the primary navigation estimator and loosely couples it with a low-fidelity orbital dynamics model (ODM), which provides auxiliary position and velocity pseudo-measurements. The contribution of the ODM is regulated through adaptive covariance assignment based on GNSS stress and the residual consistency between the ODM and GNSS solutions. Under nominal conditions, OAVT preserves the accuracy advantage of VTL over the conventional scalar tracking loop. The 3D position root-mean-square error (RMSE) is reduced from 2.631\,m for STL to 1.081\,m, while the 3D velocity RMSE decreases from 0.3985\,m/s to 0.1023\,m/s. Under degraded conditions, OAVT provides substantially greater robustness than both STL and standalone VTL. The 3D position RMSE remains bounded at 8.27\,m during a complete signal outage, 10.17\,m during gradual signal loss and reacquisition, and 26.65\,m under variable visibility, whereas STL fails to produce valid solutions and standalone VTL loses lock. These results demonstrate that OAVT substantially improves solution robustness and state continuity with only a moderate increase in computational burden, making it suitable for CubeSat orbit determination and future LEO-PNT missions.

Systems and Control.title: Counterfactual Public Opinion Projection for Intervention Decision-Making
Systems and Control.summary: Effective public opinion intervention requires forecasts of how the same event would evolve under alternative actions. Existing methods mainly capture observational associations and inadequately address treatment selection bias. The paper proposes a counterfactual public opinion projection framework for intervention decision making. Each intervention is represented by its timing, type, content and intensity. Causal triggering structures are inferred from propagation event sequences. Counterfactual trajectories of attention, sentiment and polarization are generated from adversarially balanced representations. Candidate interventions are then compared through repeated rollouts. Semisynthetic experiments yielded an overall F1 comparable to a direct structure learning baseline and a recall of 0.698 for causal edges linking semantically dissimilar content. Representation diagnostics showed that the gradient reversal layer reduced treatment information leakage from 0.163 to 0.140. Bootstrap analyses of real data further revealed intervention specific model effects on attention, sentiment and polarization.

Systems and Control.title: Semantic Anchor Communication System for Point Cloud Transmission in Internet of Vehicles
Systems and Control.summary: Joint transmission of point cloud geometry and semantics under bandwidth constraints is required for cooperative perception in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Per-point semantics cannot be explicitly preserved by existing geometric compression methods, while interpretable three-dimensional point sets cannot be directly reconstructed via task-feature communication. The paper proposes a spatial semantic anchor communication system. Distinct from global codewords and task features, anchors with explicit coordinates are employed as transmission units. Local shape descriptors and category labels are bound to a unified spatial reference, preserving the correspondence between local position, shape and semantics. At the transmitter, anchor representations are extracted and then converted into digital frames through fixed-point quantization and lossless compression.Atthereceiver,labeledpoint clouds are reconstructed through anchor-constrained local expansion, and pose-aligned multi-view observations are fused. On the 500-frame SemanticPOSS test set, the results demonstrate that spatial semantic anchors enable interpretable joint reconstruction and fusion of geometry and semantics with low transmission overhead.

Systems and Control.title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
Systems and Control.summary: AI compute is becoming large and fast-changing electrical loads. Its impacts on data center infrastructure and power grids depend not only on total energy consumption, but also on how their power draw moves over sub-second to minute timescales, including peaks, ramps, and synchronized fluctuations across accelerators. Existing energy benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) report aggregate quantities such as joules per token and rarely release the underlying time-series measurements, leaving these power dynamics poorly characterized and difficult to model. We introduce LLM-PowerTrace, an open dataset of time-resolved, per-GPU power traces for LLM fine-tuning and inference, sampled every 100\,ms on varying NVIDIA platforms paired with complete workload and system metadata. For fine-tuning, LLM-PowerTrace profiles open model families spanning a wide range of model sizes and fine-tuning methods, together with controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing. For inference, it covers variations in concurrency, GPU frequency, KV-cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request-arrival patterns. LLM-PowerTrace profiles a set of open model families across a wide range of model sizes, and controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing for fine-tuning, and it sweeps concurrency, GPU frequency, KV cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request arrival patterns for inference. Built upon power traces, we define power-grid-facing metrics as well as AI-compute power\&energy scaling law for extrapolating beyond the measured settings. Together, LLM-PowerTrace provides a dataset foundation for modeling, forecasting, and managing the fast-changing electrical behavior of AI compute.
Systems and Control.comment: In Submission; Code and dataset are available at https://systems-power-review.github.io/training-power-trace-explorer/

Systems and Control.title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
Systems and Control.summary: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.
Systems and Control.comment: 22 pages, 4 tables. Adds a fixed-fraction limit and updates the discussion of two-comparison results

Systems and Control.title: A Lyapunov-Based Small-Gain Theorem for Fixed-Time ISS: Theory, Optimization, and Games
Systems and Control.summary: We develop a Lyapunov-based small-gain theorem for establishing fixed-time input-to-state stability (FxT-ISS) guarantees in interconnected nonlinear dynamical systems. The proposed framework considers interconnections in which each subsystem admits a FxT-ISS Lyapunov function, providing robustness with respect to external inputs. We show that, under an appropriate nonlinear small-gain condition, the overall interconnected system inherits the FxT-ISS property. In this sense, the proposed result complements existing Lyapunov-based smallgain theorems for asymptotic and finite-time stability, and enables a systematic analysis of interconnection structures exhibiting fixed-time stability. To illustrate the applicability of the theory, we study feedback-based optimization problems with time-varying cost functions, and Nash-equilibrium seeking for noncooperative games with nonlinear dynamical plants in the loop. For both problems, we present a class of non-smooth gradient or pseudogradient-based controllers that achieve fixed-time convergence without requiring time-scale separation and using real-time feedback. Numerical examples are provided to validate the theoretical findings.

Systems and Control.title: Reachability-Augmented Dual Dynamic Programming for Optimal Path Parameterization
