(i) Stochastic Responses: Even with the same recommendation feed, the same user may produce different browsing responses, yielding distinct behavioral trajectories. A logged trajectory records only one such realization. (ii) Sparse Key Events: Clicks and likes provide important feedback but occur sparsely within browsing trajectories dominated by progression actions such as scrolling. Many stepwise simulators predict these actions in a dense sequence, where key events contribute relatively few training targets. To address these challenges, we propose BrowseFlow, a conditional discrete flow matching method for generative user simulation. For Sparse Key Events, BrowseFlow represents each response by its browsing extent and an ordered sequence of key events, directly modeling their counts and locations under exposure constraints. BrowseFlow learns the conditional distribution of complete browsing responses through probabilistic extent prediction and discrete flow matching over key events. Random event retention defines probability paths over partial event sequences, while transition rate matching learns stochastic insertion dynamics. For Stochastic Responses, we use the energy score, a proper scoring rule, to evaluate response fidelity and generated variability, complemented by the Wasserstein distance between key event count distributions. We further introduce TaobaoBrowse, a benchmark pairing real recommendation contexts with fine-grained browsing trajectories. Experiments across three datasets demonstrate that BrowseFlow consistently achieves the best distributional performance.

Information Retrieval.title: Defining Page-Centric Visual Document Retrieval and Evaluating Existing Benchmarks
Information Retrieval.summary: In modern information retrieval (IR), documents are increasingly encountered as structured sequences of visually rich, paginated units, rather than as flat text. Example documents encountered in our daily life include Word files, PDFs, and slide decks. Free text-centric retrieval systems either ignore this structure entirely or destroy it through arbitrary passage chunking. In this paper, we formulate page-centric Visual Document Retrieval (VDR) with pages as the fundamental indexing units and document context available for assessing page relevance. The formulation distinguishes two retrieval granularities, page and document, and three retrieval paradigms: independent-item, evidence-set, and iterative retrieval. We then assess 42 benchmarks using eight criteria covering corpus characteristics, query construction, relevance annotation, and ranking support. Our analysis shows two main findings on current VDR research. First, evaluation remains concentrated on page-level independent-item retrieval, with fewer resources supporting document-level, evidence-set, and iterative settings. Second, queries originating from real user information needs independently of target corpus content and graded relevance judgments are uncommon, while the coverage and verification of relevance judgments vary substantially. Both findings reveal gaps between the capabilities applications require and those existing evaluation protocols can establish. We provide benchmark selection guidance and identify priorities for future benchmark design, emphasizing alignment between task requirements, relevance semantics, and evaluation protocols.

Information Retrieval.title: Pix2Evidence: A Multimodal RAG System for Text and Visual Evidence
Information Retrieval.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over visually rich documents must find both relevant content and the evidence that supports an answer. Screenshot retrieval preserves images and page structure, but written facts within screenshots also need to be searchable. Moreover, topical relevance alone does not identify which retrieved tile contains evidence for the answer. We introduce Pix2Evidence, a multimodal RAG system that encodes each screenshot tile together with its available transcription into a single fused image--text representation, so that layout and readable text are considered jointly during retrieval. To guide evidence selection, a vision-language teacher describes the visible content that supports each training question. We use these descriptions to adapt the retriever, then rerank the retrieved candidates before answer generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Pix2Evidence outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Across five widely-used Wikipedia QA benchmarks, the non-reranked Pix2Evidence leads the main comparison in answer accuracy on four. On MMSearch, it reaches 26.0\%, 4.4 percentage points above PixelRAG. We will release the code and share derived data where licensing and privacy reviews permit.

Information Retrieval.title: MILES-Rec: Uncovering Implicit Intents from Mobility Behaviors for Cross-Domain POI Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Map applications bridge everyday mobility with local services, creating opportunities to recommend places by uncovering users' implicit intents. However, utility-driven map interactions provide only indirect and incomplete evidence of consumption demands, making it challenging to infer personalized service needs from observed behaviors. We propose MILES-Rec, a cross-domain POI recommendation framework that infers latent service intents from heterogeneous map behaviors and expresses them as prioritized natural language queries. It first learns from progressive reasoning demonstrations that synthesize user profiles and map histories for situation understanding, intent expansion, and query prioritization. We then introduce intent-aligned group relative policy optimization, using subsequent user interactions to reward query relevance and ranked service coverage while penalizing redundancy and excessive response length. A two-level credit assignment mechanism integrates shared list-level advantages with query-specific advantages, coordinating individual query quality with the complementary coverage of the complete query list. We further construct MILES-Bench from real user interaction logs on a large-scale mapping platform, supporting training and evaluation across diverse services under rich and sparse behavioral histories. Extensive experiments against general-purpose LLMs and specialized recommendation baselines demonstrate superior POI retrieval utility and strong service and semantic alignment, with consistent gains from behavioral policy optimization across four backbone scales.

Information Retrieval.title: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative recommendation (GR) reformulates item retrieval as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs), offering a unified paradigm for personalized recommendation. GR4AD, as an industrial generative recommendation framework, has greatly improved advertising revenue while enabling efficient real-time serving in Kuaishou. However, continued deployment has exposed three limitations: deterministic SID assignment remains sensitive to semantic boundaries; conventional backbone scaling provides diminishing revenue gains under strict serving constraints; and sequence-level value optimization provides limited credit assignment to intermediate SID decisions, causing likelihood-based beam search to prematurely prune potentially high-value candidates. We present GR4AD-X, which addresses these limitations through reliable SID construction, serving-efficient capacity scaling, and unified value alignment. Specifically, GR4AD-X improves SID reliability through Multi-Path assignment. It expands model capacity along multiple complementary dimensions rather than relying solely on wider or deeper backbones, achieving a better effectiveness-efficiency trade-off under strict serving constraints. Finally, Unified Value-Guided Generation and Discrimination (UniVGD) aligns generation with commercial value through prefix-level reward optimization, value-guided beam pruning, and discriminative reranking within a unified model. Large-scale online A/B tests on the Kuaishou advertising platform demonstrate that GR4AD-X achieves a cumulative revenue improvement of 3.07% over the deployed GR4AD baseline while satisfying strict latency and throughput constraints.

Information Retrieval.title: Time Will Tell: Harness Time to Denoise Collaborative Filtering
Information Retrieval.summary: Neural graph collaborative filtering is a powerful tool for recommendation due to its superb capability of capturing the user-item interaction. Despite the substantial progress, the noisy nature of interaction data remains a significant challenge in collaborative filtering, especially for data collected from implicit feedback. Both noisy interactions and interactions crafted by malicious users could greatly degenerate model performance. To purify the input data and enhance model robustness, it is vital to understand how noisy interactions can be identified and rectified. Existing denoising methods focus on mining the correlation between user/item embeddings and noisy interactions, neglecting the temporal dimension for denoising. However, time information bears its natural and unique advantage in revealing noisy edges as we observe in this paper. In this work, we introduce a simple yet effective mechanism for generating time-aware user/item embeddings that capture both global preferences and temporal patterns. Two strategies, reweighting adjacency matrix (Tint-A) and reweighting loss function (Tint-L), are proposed to leverage the embeddings for the task of using \underline{t}ime \underline{in}forma\underline{t}ion to denoise \underline{c}ollaborative \underline{f}iltering (TintCF). Extensive experiments have been conducted on four real-world datasets to demonstrate the efficacy of our methods and illustrate how time information indeed helps identify and rectify noisy edges. Our codes are available at \href{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}.

Information Retrieval.title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
Information Retrieval.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation is becoming agentic. A search harness writes queries, reads results, reformulates, and decides when to stop. This largely solves accuracy: a harness with only BM25/grep and MiniMax M3 answers 85% of BrowseComp-Plus and 91% on multi-hop FRAMES in our runs, without compiled or vector indexes. It exposes a context problem: an undisciplined loop repeats queries, rereads documents, and fills the window with unused passages. The missing layer is knowledge compilation: a configurable ingestion pipeline where LLMs enrich documents with context no chunk contains alone--navigation hierarchies with claim-evidence leaves, entity graphs, timelines, mind maps, ontologies, wikis, and memory. Compilation is not a better retriever: under a competent harness, structural artifacts gave no detectable accuracy gain on FRAMES, and a PageIndex-style outline degraded at scale. It is a supply layer. A navigation tree whose leaves are claim-evidence pairs--the mechanism we measure--cuts query tokens by 91% when evidence suffices and adds 1.9% when it does not, a 38% average reduction; this implies a 2% break-even sufficiency rate and a measured rate near 43%. A decision gate cuts latency from 140 s to 30 s, though substitution's token saving is bought with retrieval rounds and carries its own latency cost. Other artifacts--ontology, graph, wiki, timeline, mind map, memory--pay off in deployment (governance, integration, onboarding, temporal orientation, continuity) where accuracy benchmarks cannot see them. We describe RAGFlow's pipeline and harness (open source at https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow), which turns the loop into five disciplined stations and keeps the context entering the model the smallest sufficient set; together they form an agent-native database: a store that hands the agent compiled, governed context instead of a ranked list of passages.

Information Retrieval.title: AuthRank: Scoring Source Credibility to Counter Poisoning in CTI LLM Pipelines
Information Retrieval.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) pipelines have become essential for processing Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) to quickly extract updated threat information from open source feeds and reports for real time processing. However, these pipelines are susceptible to poisoning attacks, and previously proposed defenses can fail for CTI contexts as cyber threat information is often completely novel, and attackers can easily mimic the stylistic conventions. We propose that the robustness of LLM pipelines can be improved by applying source credibility algorithms on document corpora, using PageRank as an example. We introduce AuthRank, a credibility score computed from citation networks built using explicit citations, LLM-inferred citations, and claim-level entailment, enhanced with time decay and author credibility. Our experiments on the standardized MS MARCO dataset demonstrate improved accuracy under poisoning, and we show proof-of-concept performance on CTI documents and feeds.
Information Retrieval.comment: In Proceedings of IEEE ACSAC Workshop on AI for Cyber Threat Intelligence (WAITI) 2026

Information Retrieval.title: Automated grounding verification of AI statements about chest radiographs
Information Retrieval.summary: A grounding verifier checks a statement about a patient's image against the radiology report and the cited evidence. The state-of-the-art methods for testing these verifiers remove or replace the cited evidence while the patient's report stays unchanged. To our knowledge, no existing method checks both the report and the cited evidence. We present Building Report And Citation Examples (BRACE), an automated framework that builds training examples from public radiology reports and Radiopaedia articles. We compared a lexical baseline and 42 verifiers with 0.1-284B parameters on 5 different public chest radiograph datasets. At a threshold accepting 0.90 of the supported test examples, verifiers trained with BRACE accepted a mean of only 0.239 of AI-written statements contradicted by the report. Verifiers trained without contradicted examples passed the state-of-the-art tests, yet accepted most of these statements (0.830 on average). With citations retrieved from held-out Radiopaedia articles, verifiers trained with BRACE accepted 0.169 of AI-written statements with an agreeing report and an unsupporting citation. By contrast, zero-shot large language models mostly checked the report and not the citation (they accepted 0.830 of these statements). We further assessed the framework manually, with two board-certified radiologists independently labeling a sample of test reports. The framework's labels agreed with each radiologist (k > 0.910) almost as closely as the radiologists agreed with each other (k = 0.952). Moreover, instantiating the framework for food allergens in recipes, we showed that it extends beyond clinical applications. A verifier built the same way accepted 0.493 of the statements contradicted by the recipe, whereas a lexical baseline accepted 0.898. Using both the report and the cited evidence, verifiers trained with BRACE could check AI statements before clinicians read them.

Information Retrieval.title: Matryoshka Hash Representations for Model-Aware Compact Semantic Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) depends on dense retrieval: each document is stored as a learned vector, and queries are answered by nearest-neighbor search. Keeping one full-precision vector per document dominates index cost at corpus scale, so systems replace each vector with a short code of a few bytes (quantization). Standard quantizers such as product quantization (PQ) pick the code that best reconstructs the original vector, but reconstruction is only a proxy for retrieval: at a few bytes per document, a model-aware code trained on the retriever's ranking signal uses the budget better. A single code is even more useful if its short prefixes are each directly searchable, letting a deployment set its efficiency-quality operating point without re-encoding the corpus. But training all prefixes under one objective makes the early bits a compromise across budgets: short codes improve while the full-width code degrades. Binary codes sharpen the conflict, since a gradient step either flips a stored bit or leaves it unchanged. We introduce Matryoshka Hash Representations (MHR), a two-stage procedure that separates full-width training from prefix organization. MHR first learns a longer binary code, then freezes the model and trains zero-initialized residual code adaptors for directly searchable prefixes. Documents are stored at one bit per coordinate, queries keep continuous logits as in PQ, and search runs on FAISS FastScan. Trained on MS MARCO and zero-shot transferred to seven BEIR datasets, one MHR code reaches 0.502 NDCG@10 at 16 bytes and 0.556 at 32 bytes, against 0.404 and 0.524 for the best compact baselines; the gains hold across training seeds, on all 13 public BEIR datasets, and against off-the-shelf binary Matryoshka embeddings with stronger backbones. The same code also helps shortlist candidates for reranking and prune low-storage graph indexes such as LEANN.

Information Retrieval.title: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. A common approach is compaction, where the model replaces its history with a self-generated note. Yet off-the-shelf agentic models, including GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.3, often write ineffective notes, and reinforcement learning (RL) alone rarely discovers useful note-taking behavior. We present MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B and trained to manage its context through compaction. We first bootstrap note-taking by fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, then reinforce it with RL using a reward that combines answer correctness, note-quality heuristics, and confidence calibration. Although trained only to compact into a fresh window, MEMENTO extends at test time to strategies such as context folding and confidence-based backtracking. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, with books of up to 2.5M tokens, MEMENTO raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context. It outperforms GPT-5.5 agent in the same harness (13.1%) and full book context (56.7%) at less than 1/50 the cost. It also nearly matches a ~100x larger GLM-5.3 agent (69.3%) at 1/9 the cost, and comes within 6.4 points of GLM-5.3 full context at 1/26 the cost.

Information Retrieval.title: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
Information Retrieval.summary: Researchers often need web corpora that are not answers to a single query, but reusable collections of documents spanning many decentralized sources. We refer to this problem as thematic web data collection: assembling semantically relevant documents that share a common theme but are scattered across heterogeneous and structurally disconnected regions of the web. Existing approaches, including traversal-based methods and LLM-driven web agents, are limited by local exploration or short-horizon stopping, preventing comprehensive collection. We formulate this task as a long-horizon information foraging problem over query-induced semantic patches, where the central challenge is deciding when to continue local exploitation and when to switch to new regions. We propose PatchScout, a multi-agent framework that instantiates a class of patch-switching policies to balance local exploitation and adaptive patch switching under a fixed budget. Experiments on four live-web topics show that PatchScout substantially improves yield and domain coverage over traversal-based and search-augmented reasoning agent baselines. In an applied social science setting with an incomplete prior collection, PatchScout discovers 102 previously unidentified entities, illustrating its ability to expand existing thematic datasets.
Information Retrieval.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, to be published in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2026

Multimedia.title: Understanding the Performance Plateau in Text-to-Video Retrieval: A Comprehensive Empirical and Linguistic Analysis
Multimedia.summary: Text-to-video retrieval enables users to find relevant video content using natural language queries, a task that has grown increasingly important with the rapid expansion of online video. Over the past six years, research has produced numerous methods, such as dual encoders, attention-driven models, and multimodal fusion approaches; however, fundamental questions remain about model behavior, dataset influence, and query difficulty. In this work, we evaluate 14 state-of-the-art retrieval methods across 3 widely used datasets under a unified preprocessing and evaluation framework. We analyze caption characteristics, including length, clarity, semantic category, and Action vs. Scene balance, and link these to model performance. Our results show that short, clear, and simple captions, such as those describing single actions or color attributes, achieve higher recall, while complex events, multi-step activities, or fine-grained scene descriptions remain challenging for all existing models. Attention-driven architectures better handle temporally dependent or multi-step queries, whereas dual-encoder and multimodal fusion models perform well primarily on simpler or single-category captions. Cross-dataset generalization improves with larger, more diverse caption sets, but generative captions do not consistently enhance retrieval accuracy. Overall, our findings highlight key dataset factors, benchmark challenges, and the interplay between query content and model architecture, providing guidance for developing more effective text-to-video retrieval systems.
Multimedia.comment: Survey, 50 pages, 15 figures, 13 tables, 154 citations

Multimedia.title: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Communication
Multimedia.summary: We introduce Video Conferencing 1000 (VC-1K), an open-source test set comprising approximately 1,000 video sequences specifically designed for evaluating video processing and encoding pipelines in real-time communication (RTC) scenarios. Unlike existing test sets that primarily rely on studio-produced or screen content, VC-1K consists of user-generated video call content captured on consumer mobile devices under a wide variety of conditions. The dataset predominantly features talking-head sequences with distinct faces, but also includes a small subset of outward-facing, rear-camera videos without faces to reflect additional common RTC use cases. It spans a wide range of real-world variables including device type, lighting conditions, motion levels, indoor/outdoor environments, and demographic diversity. All video sequences are accompanied by synchronous audio to facilitate multimodal research. We detail the dataset's design methodology and statistical distribution, and demonstrate its utility through a comparative encoder evaluation of OpenH264, SVT-AV1, and libaom under constant bitrate (CBR) encoding at resolutions typical of RTC deployments. Furthermore, two super-resolution approaches, RealESRGAN and GFPGAN, are evaluated on VC-1K, highlighting the dataset as a useful benchmark for pre- and post-processing research. VC-1K is intended to serve as a publicly available dataset for the video RTC research community.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Visual Communications and Image Processing (VCIP 2026)

Image and Video Processing.title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
Image and Video Processing.summary: Radiologists' visual attention can supervise medical image learning, but how reader panel composition affects its value remains untested. We evaluated GazeRIB (Gaze-guided Radiologist-Informed Blackout), which masks unviewed regions during training and uses unmasked images at inference. Eight experts repeatedly read the same 80 chest X-rays (CXRs). We compared individual readers with three-, five- and eight-reader panels across seven architectures and 10 seeds, evaluating 910 models on a separate 2,897-CXR cohort for four-class severity prediction. Every panel improved macro F1 over the no-gaze baseline by 5.33-7.47 percentage points (pp; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.007); no individual reader reached significance on this endpoint. Three readers captured 73-80% of the eight-reader gain in macro F1, the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AU-PRC). On external validation without retraining, all four panels improved ROC-AUC on SIIM-FISABIO-RSNA by +1.93 to +4.24 pp (p <= 0.004); on MIMIC-Eye no panel differed significantly from baseline, whereas the single-reader average declined (-1.40 pp, p = 0.008). Reader composition therefore influenced performance, although transfer depended on the cohort.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 20 pages on main manuscripts (3 tables + 4 figures), 14 pages supplementary (10 tables + 8 figures)

Image and Video Processing.title: Integrating AI for Human-Centric Breast Cancer Diagnostics: A Multi-Scale and Multi-View Swin Transformer Framework
Image and Video Processing.summary: Despite advancements in Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems, breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths among women worldwide. Recent breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have shown significant promise in development of advanced Deep Learning (DL) architectures for breast cancer diagnosis through mammography. In this context, the paper focuses on the integration of AI within a Human-Centric workflow to enhance breast cancer diagnostics. Key challenges are, however, largely overlooked such as reliance on detailed tumor annotations and susceptibility to missing views, particularly during test time. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid, multi-scale and multi-view Swin Transformer-based framework (MSMV-Swin) that enhances diagnostic robustness and accuracy. The proposed MSMV-Swin framework is designed to work as a decision-support tool, helping radiologists analyze multi-view mammograms more effectively. More specifically, the MSMV-Swin framework leverages the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to isolate the breast lobe, reducing background noise and enabling comprehensive feature extraction. The multi-scale nature of the proposed MSMV-Swin framework accounts for tumor-specific regions as well as the spatial characteristics of tissues surrounding the tumor, capturing both localized and contextual information. The integration of contextual and localized data ensures that MSMV-Swin's outputs align with the way radiologists interpret mammograms, fostering better human-AI interaction and trust. A hybrid fusion structure is then designed to ensure robustness against missing views, a common occurrence in clinical practice when only a single mammogram view is available.

Image and Video Processing.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision
Image and Video Processing.summary: With the surge of machine vision applications, image compression for both machine and human vision (ICMH) has become an important research area. Existing studies mainly focus on task-specific adaptation or multi-task joint optimization, yet they often overlook the unequal contributions of different features and network layers to downstream machine vision tasks. To address this issue, we first quantitatively investigate the impact of different feature and network layers on machine vision performance, providing a principled understanding of their importance. Based on this analysis, an Importance Guided feature and network Dual Adaptation (IGDA) framework is developed for ICMH. It adopts implicit neural representation as the basic architecture and designs an efficient adaptation structure with both feature and network weight adaptation. An Importance-Guided Network Adaptation (IGNA) module is developed with a low-rank adaptation strategy to selectively adjust key network layers according to their importance in different tasks. An Importance-Guided Feature Adaptation (IGFA) module is developed with a low-rank and Kronecker product-based transform to explore the non-local property of the features in order to reduce the number of adaptation parameters. Extensive experiments on representative machine vision tasks, including image classification and object detection, demonstrate that our IGDA-ICMH framework achieves significantly better performance than the existing implicit neural representation-based methods for ICMH.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Published in IEEE TCSVT

Image and Video Processing.title: Sample-wise Constrained Learning via a Sequential Penalty Approach with Applications in Image Processing
Image and Video Processing.summary: In many learning tasks, certain requirements on the processing of individual data samples can arguably be formalized, in an intelligible way, as strict constraints of the underlying optimization problem, rather than by means of arbitrary penalties that often require heavy trial-and-error tuning. In this paper we show that, in these scenarios, learning can be carried out exploiting a sequential penalty method that allows to explicitly deal with constraints. For the proposed algorithm we show that, under classical assumptions and in the considered learning scenario, penalty subproblems can provably be solved in finite time with suitable guarantees of approximate stationarity in expectation; we also show that, when the latter condition is guaranteed for the subproblems, the overall sequential scheme possesses almost sure convergence properties to KKT-stationary points of (general) constrained problems. The results of experiments on sandbox and real-world image processing tasks show that the method is indeed viable to be used in practical deep learning scenarios.
Image and Video Processing.comment: https://openreview.net/forum?id=Xi1UWSFooI

Image and Video Processing.title: Enhancing Medical Lesion Segmentation via Several Simple Modules
Image and Video Processing.summary: This work introduces three lightweight enhancement modules for medical lesion segmentation to improve clinical applicability, particularly under data-scarce and computationally constrained environments. Current mainstream methods struggle with the lack of high-quality annotations for rare pathologies, which often leads to severe morphological distortions during inference, despite achieving seemingly ideal DSC scores. Furthermore, the isolated development of individual segmentation tasks restricts cross-domain methodological innovation, underscoring the need for leveraging shared knowledge across different lesions within the same anatomical region. However, constrained access to historical data and annotations hinders efficient knowledge extraction and triggers catastrophic forgetting when adapting to new classes. To address these challenges, we first propose DT-Morph Combined Loss with continuous spatial pooling to optimize differentiable topological structures and boundary continuity. Second, we introduce 3D Group Prompt, which extracts domain-universal knowledge via curated volumetric image-mask alignment prompts together with text prompts built on SAT baseline. Finally, we replace conventional output layers with Many-to-One Conditional Segmentation Head equipped with synonym-resolved routing, which brings negligible computational cost and enables fast incremental learning for new categories without sacrificing performance on old tasks. Ablation studies on abdominal and extra-abdominal datasets covering both organ and lesion segmentation verify the efficacy of our modules.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: TopoHyperClinicalGraph: A Geometry and Topology-Aware Multimodal Framework for Cancer Survival Prediction
Image and Video Processing.summary:
We developed TopoHyperClinicalGraph, a multimodal framework combining hyperbolic tissue geometry, persistent topology and clinical graph learning for cancer survival prediction. Pre-extracted UNI2-h features are reduced from 1,536 to 1,024 dimensions using training-fold PCA. A pathology backbone combines hyperbolic neighborhoods with Lorentz-centroid attention pooling. Once frozen, its survival logits are adjusted using persistence descriptors from up to 64 landmarks per slide and sampling controls. A five-node clinical graph then learns a further correction from age, sex, stage, T and N.
  Five-fold patient-level evaluation covered eight TCGA and CPTAC cohorts with 2,364 patients. Mean validation-selected C-indices for TopoHyperClinicalGraph versus pathology-only spatial PatchGCN were 0.7563 versus 0.7386 in COADREAD, 0.6220 versus 0.5998 in HNSC, 0.6755 versus 0.6535 in BRCA and 0.6409 versus 0.6176 in STAD. CPTAC scores were 0.5984 in HNSC, 0.6060 in PDA, 0.8055 in CCRCC and 0.7192 in LUAD. CPTAC-HNSC used TCGA-initialized adaptation; other CPTAC backbones were trained within their cohorts. Geometry accounted for most pathology-only gains, with smaller persistence effects. Clinical graph fusion exceeded its matched node-wise control in five cohorts, tied in one and scored lower in two; clinical-only prediction exceeded fusion in three CPTAC cohorts.
  The framework supports separate evaluation of geometric, topological and clinical contributions. All scores were validation-selected; independent testing is needed to establish generalizability.

Image and Video Processing.title: The Generalized Twin Image: Understanding Regularized Phase Retrieval
Image and Video Processing.summary: Image priors can dramatically improve phase retrieval reconstruction, but their effectiveness strongly varies between imaging modalities. We introduce the generalized twin image, which extends the classical twin-image ambiguity from Fourier phase retrieval to any invertible sensing operator, to understand this effectiveness. The ambiguity extends to undersampled and oversampled measurements, remaining exact under undersampling and for oversampled coded Fourier measurements. We show that it provides a simple criterion to assess regularization effectiveness: the image prior should favor the ground truth over its generalized twin image. We propose the total-variation ratio as a simple measure of this preference, and derive closed-form estimates for structured random phase retrieval models. Experiments with a pretrained denoiser demonstrate that the ratio predicts regularized reconstruction performance across different sensing models.

Image and Video Processing.title: PRIN: A Perceptual-Structural Retinex-Inspired Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement
Image and Video Processing.summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) focuses not only on visibility recovery but also on preserving structurally meaningful content and perceptual naturalness. Existing learning-based methods may achieve favorable pixel-wise fidelity while still producing over-smoothed textures, color deviations, or spatially incoherent illumination. Retinex-inspired methods provide interpretable decomposition into reflectance and illumination components, however, the asymmetric restoration roles of these components are rarely encoded through branch-specific frequency-domain refinement. To address this issue, we propose a Perceptual-Structural Retinex-Inspired Network (PRIN), which integrates Retinex priors with restoration-role-aware enhancement. PRIN employs a shared encoder and asymmetric decoders to estimate reflectance and illumination components. The reflectance branch performs attention-guided and edge-aware wavelet refinement to preserve textures and boundaries, whereas the illumination branch promotes spatially coherent brightness adjustment. After the recomposition of reflectance and illumination branches, a curve-based post-composition enhancement head calibrates residual tone and exposure deviations. Experiments on LOL-v1, LOL-v2-Syn, and LOL-v2-Real show that the proposed network ties for the best structural similarity index (SSIM) and obtains the second-lowest learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) on LOL-v1, achieves the best SSIM and LPIPS on LOL-v2-Syn, and obtains the highest peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and the second-lowest LPIPS on LOL-v2-Real.

Image and Video Processing.title: Bayesian PET Reconstruction with Learned Flow Matching Priors via Langevin Sampling
Image and Video Processing.summary: Image reconstruction for positron emission tomography (PET) is a challenging inverse problem due to its inherent ill-posedness and Poisson counting noise, particularly in low-dose acquisitions. In this work, we introduce a novel Bayesian PET reconstruction framework that leverages a flow-matching generative prior learned from high-quality PET images. By incorporating this prior, we formulate PET reconstruction as a Bayesian inference problem and solve it via latent-space posterior sampling using the unadjusted Langevin algorithm. We evaluate the proposed method through numerical experiments and benchmark it against classical reconstruction methods and state-of-the-art deep learning-based baselines. The proposed method achieves improved reconstruction performance while enabling posterior uncertainty quantification.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Selected as the Best Student Paper Award for 2026 IVMSP

Image and Video Processing.title: With foundation-model features, aggregator complexity does not improve cross-hospital discrimination in gastric whole-slide image classification
Image and Video Processing.summary: Whole-slide image classifiers are usually developed within one hospital and often go untested at unseen hospitals. We assembled 5,036 haematoxylin-and-eosin-stained gastric slides from five Korean hospitals, scanned at 20x and 40x, and compared multiple-instance learning aggregators under leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features. A hierarchical patch-region-slide graph aggregator (CHIME-MIL) with site alignment and two-scale fusion reached a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.837, above six conventional attention and transformer aggregators trained without these steps. Under a matched recipe it did not exceed attention-based pooling, and global max pooling given the same alignment and fusion was better (AUC 0.855, P = 0.0002). The alignment, which subtracts each hospital's mean feature vector without labels, onboarded a new hospital from ten unlabelled slides and cost 0.002 AUC without held-out-hospital data, but its accuracy gains were small and inconsistent. The model had low top-label calibration error (0.053) but under-confident malignancy probabilities, and removing its most-attended patches lowered the malignancy probability far more than removing random patches. With these features, more complex aggregators did not improve discrimination; what a deployable system adds is label-free onboarding, calibration checks and auditable evidence.

Image and Video Processing.title: PBSR: Pseudo-Burst Super-Resolution via Zero-Shot Novel View Synthesis
Image and Video Processing.summary: Burst super-resolution (BSR) achieves higher reconstruction fidelity than single-image super-resolution (SISR) by aggregating sub-pixel information from multiple frames. However, it requires a burst of frames captured under near-static conditions, and such frames are unavailable for single photographs or archival images. We propose Pseudo-Burst Super-Resolution (PBSR), which brings BSR-style reconstruction to the single-image input setting by synthesizing pseudo-burst frames via zero-shot novel view synthesis (NVS). PBSR first generates pseudo-burst frames with realistic parallax using a viewpoint sampling strategy calibrated to the pixel-shift distribution of real burst datasets. The frames are then processed by a BSR backbone equipped with a geometry-aware alignment module that reuses the NVS camera parameters and estimated depth. While the NVS stage is zero-shot, the backbone is fine-tuned with an artifact-aware adaptation so that it can exploit the synthesized frames despite their generative artifacts. Experiments on the BurstSR dataset show that PBSR consistently improves in PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS over the single-frame baseline with the same reconstruction backbone.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in New Generation Computing. 17 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: Stochastic Generative Plug-and-Play Priors
Image and Video Processing.summary: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods are widely used for solving imaging inverse problems by incorporating a denoiser into an optimization algorithm. Score-based diffusion models (SBDMs) have recently demonstrated strong generative performance via a denoiser trained across a wide range of noise levels. Despite their shared reliance on denoisers, it remains unclear how to systematically use SBDMs as priors within the PnP framework without relying on reverse diffusion sampling. In this paper, we establish a score-based interpretation of PnP that justifies using pretrained SBDMs directly within PnP algorithms. Building on this connection, we introduce a stochastic generative PnP (SGPnP) framework that uses stochastic re-noising to better leverage the broad noise-level conditioning of pretrained SBDMs, significantly improving reconstruction quality in severely ill-posed inverse problems. We show that noise injection induces optimization on a Gaussian-smoothed objective and enables avoidance of strict saddle points under suitable conditions. Experiments on challenging inverse tasks, such as multi-coil MRI reconstruction and large-mask natural image inpainting, demonstrate consistent improvement over conventional PnP methods and achieve performance competitive with diffusion-based solvers.

Image and Video Processing.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Training-Free Empirical-Bayes Estimation
Image and Video Processing.summary: In Temporal computed tomography (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work set the resulting per-bundle limits and tested a learned prior on one patient at one incident count $N_0$; this paper lifts both. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator. V8c is a neural-network corrector trained on 19 patients stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a training-free empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles. Results use that work's Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), charging bias as error. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence (no bow-tie) baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of its incident photons, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below conventional bow-ties; the bow-tie alone achieves this median, and tube-current modulation trims the tail. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median mean-squared-error ratio 1.02); training-free T2bp$\circ$SNN2 lowers the ratio to 0.89 (0.74-1.26). It is best or tied on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm) and trails T2bp$\circ$V8c by 3% on the fourth. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired below its training count level. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and training-free estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.
Image and Video Processing.comment: v2: title changed from v1 (was "...: Flux-Compensation Design and Multi-Patient Generalization"); corpus results recomputed with the truth-free T2bp configuration; conventional bow-tie comparison and acquisition and bias-structure tests added. 72 pages (30 main text, 42 supplementary material), 8 figures, 19 tables. Paper 2 of a series; companion to arXiv:2604.10934

Image and Video Processing.title: Directional Dual-Head Supervision for Real-Time Source-Free Polyp Segmentation
Image and Video Processing.summary: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) is critical for medical image segmentation as it adapts a model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data, thereby preserving data privacy. However, its effectiveness is often limited by confirmation bias: self-training models tend to miss small polyps, hallucinate foreground, and produce imprecise contours. We propose MedRT-SFSeg, a real-time SFDA framework built on a dual-head one-to-one/one-to-many YOLO segmentation architecture. Mask-DHF fuses precision- and recall-oriented predictions into stable pseudo-instances, while DURR uses the sign of pixel-level dual-head disagreement as a directional cue to expand or shrink masks, and additionally recovers missed instances and suppresses hallucinations. Seg-MARD further regularizes feature representations through mask-guided, region-stratified sampling. Experiments on bidirectional adaptation between Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB show that MedRT-SFSeg achieves 80.43%/80.77% Dice and 5.53/8.44 mm ASD, improving the non-adapted baseline by 7.7 and 9.8 Dice points while running at more than 62 FPS end-to-end. These results suggest that segmentation-aware dual-head supervision can improve pseudo-label quality without sacrificing real-time inference. Project page: https://danielnguyen-05.github.io/MedRT-SFSeg
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted to MMM 2027

Image and Video Processing.title: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Communication
Image and Video Processing.summary: We introduce Video Conferencing 1000 (VC-1K), an open-source test set comprising approximately 1,000 video sequences specifically designed for evaluating video processing and encoding pipelines in real-time communication (RTC) scenarios. Unlike existing test sets that primarily rely on studio-produced or screen content, VC-1K consists of user-generated video call content captured on consumer mobile devices under a wide variety of conditions. The dataset predominantly features talking-head sequences with distinct faces, but also includes a small subset of outward-facing, rear-camera videos without faces to reflect additional common RTC use cases. It spans a wide range of real-world variables including device type, lighting conditions, motion levels, indoor/outdoor environments, and demographic diversity. All video sequences are accompanied by synchronous audio to facilitate multimodal research. We detail the dataset's design methodology and statistical distribution, and demonstrate its utility through a comparative encoder evaluation of OpenH264, SVT-AV1, and libaom under constant bitrate (CBR) encoding at resolutions typical of RTC deployments. Furthermore, two super-resolution approaches, RealESRGAN and GFPGAN, are evaluated on VC-1K, highlighting the dataset as a useful benchmark for pre- and post-processing research. VC-1K is intended to serve as a publicly available dataset for the video RTC research community.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Visual Communications and Image Processing (VCIP 2026)

Image and Video Processing.title: Does Vendor Image Processing Matter? Learning Echocardiography Display Appearance from Native Beamspace Data
Image and Video Processing.summary: Most echocardiography datasets contain vendor-processed images, but processing is often undocumented and may affect model performance and robustness. To address this, we train a small convolutional neural network to reproduce General Electric display appearance from native beamspace brightness-mode ultrasound, using 8 406 recordings from 605 unique patients. The beamspace CNN reduces test mean absolute error by 43% over the optimal pointwise brightness map, outperforms an equivalent Cartesian CNN and runs in real time on a CPU. Across the EchoXFlow and CAMUS datasets, unfiltered training followed by filtered evaluation yields the lowest mean Dice for every class, suggesting filtering may be useful as augmentation when evaluation data are filtered or their processing is unknown. Code and pretrained weights: https://github.com/Ahus-AIM/EchoAppearance

Image and Video Processing.title: A Rate-Distortion Optimized Skip Mode Coding Framework for Neural Video Compression in AVS
Image and Video Processing.summary: With the development of deep learning, neural video compression (NVC) is gaining increasing interest and is currently under standardization in the AVS (Audio Video Coding Standard). Skip mode coding, a crucial component in the traditional video compression, is also adopted in AVS NVC. Although the skip mode takes a large portion in encoding the motion and residual features in the NVC, there is a lack of investigation on the rate distortion performance of the skip mode coding. In this paper, we first thoroughly investigate the rate and distortion distribution in the skip mode coding within a spatial frame and under different temporal reference qualities, and demonstrate that distortion distribution changes spatially and temporally. Therefore, a rate-distortion optimized skip mode coding (RDOSkip) framework is proposed, where the rate and distortion in the skip mode coding is formulated based on a statistical distribution predicted by the hyperprior and the Bayes' theorem. An adaptive skip mode decision method based on spatial-temporal joint RD optimization is developed for the skip mode coding among channels and frames in a group of pictures. It addresses the limitation of the rigid fixed-distortion distribution assumption in skip mode coding within the existing methods that rely on a fixed skip threshold. The temporal skip mode decision method has been adopted in the ongoing AVS NVC standard and incorporated into the reference software. The proposed RDOSkip can be directly used in the inference without any training and with negligible complexity increase. Experimental results further demonstrate that the proposed RDOSkip can improve the performance by 0.90% and 1.29% on AVS and HEVC datasets, respectively, in terms of BD-rate saving.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Published in IEEE TCSVT

Image and Video Processing.title: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
Image and Video Processing.summary: Fourier phase retrieval reconstructs images from magnitude measurements without phase information, but noise and channel ambiguities make natural color-image recovery challenging. Although diffusion-prior methods provide strong image constraints, their recovery can deteriorate under stronger measurement noise, and repeated generative updates incur substantial computational cost. This paper proposes FlowFPR, which integrates a pretrained Flow Matching prior with relaxed averaged alternating reflections for oversampled Fourier phase retrieval. Each outer iteration obtains a clean image estimate through a single time-dependent Flow prediction, applies measurement-consistency correction, and reconstructs the next path state after fusing the two candidates. This process requires no backpropagation of measurement errors through the Flow network. To address ineffective or excessive correction caused by prescribed fusion weights and fixed inner depths, we introduce adaptive fusion based on residual improvement and a controlled inner search combining early stopping with best-so-far candidate selection. Their combination yields a joint variant alongside the basic method and the two independent improvements. Experiments on natural face images under a common ground-truth-assisted multiple-restart evaluation protocol show that the joint variant achieves the best mean quality among the evaluated methods at the two tested nonzero noise levels, while same-hardware timing demonstrates lower end-to-end runtime than the diffusion-based baselines.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures

Image and Video Processing.title: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification
Image and Video Processing.summary: Chronic kidney disease is characterized by structural alterations in renal tissue and progressive loss of kidney function. While glomerular subtype ratios provide a compact and clinically meaningful summary of glomerular composition, representing pathomic information using whole-slide image (WSI)-level mean values diminishes glomerulus-level heterogeneity and the contribution of less prevalent patterns. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated whether modeling individual glomeruli using multiple-instance learning (MIL) could provide complementary information to conventional subtype ratios for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classification. We analyzed 162 kidney-biopsy WSIs from 162 patients, categorizing renal function as eGFR < 60 or >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Quantitative size, shape, intensity, and texture features were extracted from segmented glomeruli, representing each patient as a bag of glomerular instances. An attention-based MIL model was trained to aggregate these heterogeneous pathomic profiles. We evaluated subtype ratios, pathomics, and their combination using ABMIL, with a mean-pooled multilayer perceptron baseline. In five-fold cross-validation, the subtype-ratio-only model achieved an AUC of 0.7262 +/- 0.0596. MIL using pathomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.7362 +/- 0.0788, whereas integrating pathomics with subtype ratios produced the highest mean AUC of 0.7630 +/- 0.0665. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine individual feature contributions. These results demonstrate that MIL-based pathomics can complement established glomerular subtype ratios by capturing additional glomerulus-level information for quantitative kidney-biopsy analysis.

Systems and Control.title: Measurement-Based Assessment of Decadal Inertia and Primary Frequency Response Trends in the US Eastern Interconnection
Systems and Control.summary: Changes in the generation mix of the U.S. Eastern Interconnection (EI) raise questions about long-term frequency performance, particularly inertia and primary frequency response (PFR). This paper jointly examines these characteristics using synchronized FNET/GridEye frequency measurements and confirmed generation-trip events from 2013 to 2025. A representative EI frequency trajectory is constructed using the median of geographically distributed measurements. Effective inertia is estimated quarterly from the early post-disturbance rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), using a 3-second window and least-squares fitting. PFR is evaluated using the beta metric, which measures aggregate frequency response from disturbance size and the A-to-B frequency deviation. Annual beta estimates are obtained after filtering events by starting frequency and disturbance size to improve comparability across years. Results show that EI effective inertia varies seasonally and follows a non-monotonic trend rather than a uniform long-term decline. Over the same period, coal generation decreased while natural gas, wind, and solar generation increased. Changes in synchronous generator commitment and operating conditions may have offset some expected inertia reductions. Filtered beta generally increased from the mid-2010s to the early 2020s, with year-to-year variability thereafter. The different trends show that early inertial behavior and broader aggregate frequency response have not evolved in parallel. Joint analysis of inertia and beta offers a more complete measurement-based assessment of EI frequency performance during the generation transition.
Systems and Control.comment: Presented in CIGRE 2026 Grid of the Future Symposium.The paper has 12 pages and 6 figures in total

Systems and Control.title: A Hybrid Path Planning Framework for Assistive Wheelchair Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
Systems and Control.summary: Autonomous wheelchairs can improve the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments by providing greater independence. However, reliable navigation especially in human environments is a major challenge due to factors such as dynamic obstacles, unpredictable pedestrian behavior, and the users' need to complete multiple stops along the way before reaching their final destination. This paper presents a hybrid path planning framework for multi-goal navigation in dynamic environments. The framework integrates the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for global task ordering with the Potential Field (PF) method and heuristic local planners such as Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and A-star (A*) to achieve collision-free navigation. Within this hybrid framework, TSP determines the visiting order of intermediate stations, PF transfers global path information, and local planners avoid obstacles while guiding the robot to the stations. The local planners generate feasible paths that allow the robot to follow the global trajectory and reroute to avoid static and dynamic obstacles. For this purpose, two algorithms have been developed: (i) TSP-PF-RRT and (ii) TSP-PF-A*. The performance of the proposed algorithms are evaluated using Monte Carlo simulations in crowded and extra-crowded scenarios that contain heterogeneous dynamic and static obstacles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework enables efficient multi-goal navigation while maintaining safe operation in dynamic environments with humans, with TSP-PF-RRT achieving fewer or no collisions and shorter travel distances.
Systems and Control.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Presented as a main-track paper at the International Conference of Social Robotics + ART'26, London, UK, 1-4 July 2026

Systems and Control.title: System-Level Factors Influencing AGC Cyber-Attack Success and RAS Vulnerability in Multi-Area Grids
Systems and Control.summary: Automatic generation control (AGC) stabilizes frequency and scheduled power exchanges among interconnected areas, yet its reliance on communication networks introduces cyber-vulnerabilities. This work examines coordinated AGC cyber-attacks in the presence of remedial action schemes (RAS) and identifies operating conditions under which an attacker can drive grid frequency beyond safe limits while evading RAS. A feedback-based attack policy is used to manipulate AGC signals and steer system frequency toward unsafe trajectories. Then, a large nested-loop parametric sweep---spanning attacked-area inertia relative to its interconnected neighboring area, AGC capacity versus maximum tie-line transfer, AGC update rate, load damping, and bi-directional power transfers---generates over 1.45 million scenarios. These are classified using a decision tree to establish guidelines to distinguish successful from unsuccessful attacks based on frequency deviations. The resulting vulnerability guidelines are validated on a three-area system using phasor-domain simulations with IEEE 9-bus area models, detailed turbine--governor dynamics, and under/over-frequency load and generation shedding. Results show that specific combinations of AGC capacity, inertia distribution, and pre-attack tie-line loading increase the likelihood of successful attacks, offering operators actionable criteria for identifying vulnerable operating conditions.

Systems and Control.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
Systems and Control.summary: We study whether a language model can help design controllers whose behavior can be formally checked. In proof-carrying evolution (PCE), a search proposes controllers together with their certificates. Their mathematical forms are fixed; a proposer chooses their numerical parameters together. Certificate checks guide selection, and only a certified candidate can be returned. The deployed artifact is a control law and its certificate; the language model is used only during design. We compare four language models with classical search and synthesis on docking under a speed limit, pursuit of a maneuvering target, and attitude control on SO(3), using paired runs and shared proposal allowances. Certificates are checked in exact rational arithmetic during search on the linear problems. On SO(3), the search uses floating-point checks, followed by exact re-verification of every reported champion. The best run of each method also receives Lean 4 proofs of its stated control properties. On the linear problems, the strongest models beat the standard classical baselines on every run, but a classical optimizer that chooses certificates for the same objective closes most of that lead. Among the cited pursuit champions, the ranking does not survive a change from Euler to zero-order-hold dynamics. On SO(3), no model detectably outperforms CMA-ES when mixed with classical mutation. When models write every proposal, one tested model improves on CMA-ES and the other performs worse than its mixed variant. All search medians remain below the hand-tuned law. In a docking control with the objective and mutation operator held fixed, retaining certified candidates yields new certified designs in every run; removing this rule yields none.

Systems and Control.title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
Systems and Control.summary: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.
Systems and Control.comment: 32 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables, submitted to Military Operations Research

Systems and Control.title: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor
Systems and Control.summary: Spline representations provide a compact way to approximate continuous trajectories using a finite number of parameters. When approximating trajectories generated by dynamical systems, the efficiency of a spline representation depends strongly on the placement of knot points. Uniform knot distributions often lead to inefficient representations, requiring either unnecessary control points or producing poor approximations in regions where the trajectory varies rapidly. In this work we propose a learning-based method for adaptive knot placement in B-spline approximations of trajectories generated by ordinary differential equations. A neural network learns a mapping from the initial condition of the system to quantities that characterize the local variation of the resulting trajectory. These estimates are used to construct nonuniform knot distributions that approximately equidistribute a local error indicator, reducing the number of control points needed to meet a prescribed accuracy.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. This work is presented at IEEE CDC 2026

Systems and Control.title: Risk Assessment of Fair Multi-Period Dynamic Operating Envelopes under Uncertainty
Systems and Control.summary: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) can allocate time-varying export capacity to distributed energy resources (DERs), and while they are not intended to make operations immune to voltage violations, they should guide operations to mostly remain inside expected values under changing regimes and residual forecast errors. However, although recent literature proposed many different techniques for implementing DOEs, there is sparse discussion of analyzing and quantifying the risk of using more or less conservative DOEs under uncertain operating regimes. Having this gap in mind, this paper develops a risk-oriented extension of a previously established fair distributed multi-period optimal power flow (OPF) framework, where fair or technical DOEs are fixed as first-stage decisions and the OPF leverages battery energy storage and renewable curtailment as recourse under regime uncertainties. An independent nonlinear AC power flow then computes a resulting ensemble, which is summarized by (i) voltage-violation probability, severity, and a persistence metric for consecutive out-of-band hours, (ii) curtailment and Jain and Gini indices, and (iii) model deviations. Different probability situations are assessed, ranging from uniform, sunny-heavy, night-peak-heavy, and adversarial, which separate the envelope design from the assumed operating distribution. An optional outer loop allows for fine-tuning a fairness--efficiency parameter under explicit violation and persistence budgets. The combination of the outer loop and the overall framework, which quantifies how often and how severely operating limits are exceeded, creates an auditable methodology mixing equitable export allocation, distributed recourse, and AC risk assessment for active distribution network operators, and this framework is assessed using up to 1000 Monte Carlo scenarios per mixture and DOE design.

Systems and Control.title: Epidemic Forecasting and Behavioral Response Estimation with a Behavior-Coupled SEIR Model
Systems and Control.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has exhibited multiple waves of infections, reflecting feedback between disease transmission and adaptive population behavior. Accurately predicting and understanding these dynamics remains a central challenge for epidemic modeling. In this paper, we develop a forecasting framework based on a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered (SEIR) model coupled with an evolutionary model of behavioral adaptation, in which population compliance with protective measures evolves in response to perceived infection risk and associated costs. We formulate forecasting as the estimation of behavioral incentive parameters that govern the coupled behavior-disease dynamics, using hospitalization time series data together with standard assumptions on disease-related parameters. Using the inferred parameters, we generate rolling monthly forecasts of infection levels and evaluate the approach on both synthetic data and hospitalization time series from multiple U.S. states (Texas, California, Colorado, and Arizona). The proposed framework provides a principled way to incorporate behavior-disease feedback into epidemic forecasting while yielding interpretable estimates of population-level incentives.
Systems and Control.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

Systems and Control.title: Safety Verification for Voltage Control in Inverter Dominated Radial Distribution Networks under Actuator and Sensor Adversarial Attacks
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops a safety verification framework for inverter-based radial distribution networks under sensor and actuator attacks. Each customer is equipped with a droop-based controller to regulate its voltage within a desirable bound of a reference, i.e., to achieve safety. In our setting, attacks and disturbances enter the droop-based controllers, while actuator attacks corrupt the reactive power injected into the network. Consequently, invariance of the controller state alone does not guarantee compliance with inverter capacities or customer voltage limits. To address this challenge, we derive conditions to guarantee that the reactive power state remains inside a predefined ellipsoid, while at the same time ensuring that the attacked reactive power injections and customer voltages respect predetermined operating limits that hold uniformly for the entire predefined ellipsoid. Together, these conditions guarantee safety under all admissible disturbances and state-dependent sensor and actuator attacks. Finally, we express the resulting containment condition as a linear matrix inequality (LMI) feasibility problem. A five-customer radial network based on the CIGRE benchmark corroborates our theoretical developments in simulations.

Systems and Control.title: Is Your AI Fast Enough to Run a Fusion Reactor?
Systems and Control.summary: In magnetic confinement fusion, compact machine learning algorithms are often integrated into the control loop on CPU-based custom hardware stacks. Deterministic implementations of these algorithms target instabilities which can evolve over microseconds to milliseconds. Staying within this framework may therefore limit the pace of control-system development to the inference time available. With the expansion of hardware acceleration and large models, we aim to bring ML models for fusion control to modern inference engines and compare, based on the physics reactor, the suitability of each engine per model. This study implements a consistent real-time machine learning algorithm for GPUs and optimized CPU packages, including OpenVINO, XLA, and TVM, at DIII-D National Fusion Facility. For the smallest model, one CPU core responds within 3.6 $μ$s in 99% of control cycles and an NVIDIA A100 within 28 $μ$s. We also evaluate models running simultaneously, as they would run in a typical experiment, and find best use cases per framework.

Systems and Control.title: Preference-Conditioned Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Terminally Constrained Multi-Objective Control
Systems and Control.summary: Multi-objective optimal control is commonly addressed by reinforcement learning with fixed scalarization weights, requiring a separate training run and constraint enforcement for each trade-off. This letter extends critic-free group-relative policy optimization to terminally constrained multi-objective control: a single preference-conditioned policy is trained over random preferences and returns a feasible approximation of the Pareto front in one run. Three structural results are established. Group normalization after scalarization preserves the prescribed preference, whereas per-objective normalization induces policy-dependent distortion; with pairwise distinct normalization scales, only single-objective preferences remain unchanged. A positive floor prevents the terminal-constraint multiplier from vanishing and renders the penalty exact when the floor exceeds a geometric multiplier. Deterministic terminal violation is bounded by expected stochastic violation plus a term depending on terminal-state curvature and action variance, so stochastic feasibility alone does not certify deterministic execution. On a heavy-duty range-extender powertrain with six stage costs and a terminal state-of-charge band, a representative training run places all 32 preference-grid solutions in band on six cycles inside and outside the training pool. Averaged over ten runs, the method yields more in-band solutions under deterministic execution than a critic-based conditioned baseline with the same terminal-constraint handling.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Systems and Control.title: Safe Planning for Black-Box Systems via MAP Inference with Truncated Diffusion Priors and CBF-Informed Gibbs Likelihoods
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference framework with a truncated diffusion prior for safe planning (TDP-SafeMAP). Under a generalized Bayesian formulation, a criterion based on covariance condition number determines the reverse diffusion truncation timestep, and the clean control distribution predicted at that timestep is approximated by a Gaussian prior encoding the control regularities and uncertainty of expert data. An energy function containing a control barrier function (CBF) constraint violation measure defines a Gibbs task likelihood that incorporates physical constraint information. After fusing the prior and likelihood, the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), whose core update admits an interpretation as a sampling-based approximation to natural-gradient ascent, approximates the posterior mode using only black-box evaluations. Bézier-curve-based dimensionality reduction and related techniques further improve computational efficiency and task-completion capability. Theoretical analysis establishes an error bound for the approximate MAP solution, an explicit condition for CBF safety preservation, and the equivalence of the MAP problem under prior whitening. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently generates safe, smooth, and goal-reaching trajectories, providing an effective and practical statistical inference approach to safe planning for black-box systems.

Systems and Control.title: Clinical-Protocol-Aware Cyber Resilience for Connected Clinical Technologies Under AI-Enabled Adversarial Conditions
Systems and Control.summary: Healthcare increasingly relies on connected medical devices, clinical information systems, cloud services, and distributed-care technologies, creating cybersecurity risks across clinical workflows. AI-enabled capabilities can accelerate vulnerability discovery and attack-path analysis, increasing the need to limit compromise propagation. This paper proposes a clinical-protocol-aware cyber-resilience framework based on bounded clinical micro-networks and controlled interconnections. The framework integrates clinical factors into cybersecurity design, management, and evaluation, covering prevention, containment, and incident response. A parameterized Monte Carlo simulation distinguishes technical cyber exposure from modeled clinical consequence. Experiments investigate architectural connectivity, adversarial capability, security controls, protocol dependency, risk alignment, communication directionality, lifecycle integration, and response timing. Under the simulation assumptions, connected architecture increases mean cyber exposure by 56.3% relative to segmented architecture, while combined prevention and containment reduce exposure by 60.1% relative to no controls. Increasing protocol dependency raises the modeled clinical-impact index from 1.021 to 7.567 without changing mean cyber exposure, demonstrating that technical exposure and clinical consequence can diverge. Risk-alignment experiments further indicate higher modeled clinical impact when greater technical risk corresponds to greater clinical significance. The findings support comparative architectural analysis, not calibrated estimates of real-world cyber risk, control effectiveness, or patient harm. The framework provides a clinical-context-aware approach to security-boundary design, control prioritization, and coordinated containment in connected healthcare environments.
Systems and Control.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Systems and Control.title: Scaly: an Optimizing Compiler for Optimal Control
Systems and Control.summary: We present Scaly, an open-source optimizing compiler for optimal control, written in Python, that generates fast C code. Scaly provides a modeling language embedded in Python for the parametric optimization problems that arise in model predictive control and moving horizon estimation, and computes the sparse derivatives that standard optimization solvers need. Scaly accepts general nonlinear programs but applies optimizations specific to optimal control, which preserve the repeated structure of a problem, such as the stages of a horizon, through differentiation down to the generated loops. The generated C depends only on the C math library and never allocates memory dynamically. On three benchmark problems, Scaly evaluates the Hessian of the Lagrangian up to 26 times faster than CasADi, with smaller binaries and build times that stay nearly constant with the horizon. With the same solver, Scaly shortens the solver time per control step on every benchmark, by a factor of up to 9.

Systems and Control.title: SmartMeterFM: Flow Matching for Smart Meter Data Generation, Imputation, and Super-Resolution Without Retraining
Systems and Control.summary: Distribution system operators need realistic load and generation profiles when measurements are unavailable, incomplete, or too coarse for the intended analysis. Training separate models for synthetic data generation, imputation, and super-resolution can duplicate modeling effort as observation requirements change. This paper presents SmartMeterFM, a conditional flow matching model trained once on monthly smart meter profiles at 15 min resolution. Customer and calendar attributes condition the model during training, while numerical profile constraints, observed intervals, and coarse measurements are incorporated through projection-based guidance at inference. The same weights serve all tasks without task-specific retraining and preserve temporal patterns and extreme values while producing profiles consistent with the supplied observations. A large-scale case study using Dutch consumption and photovoltaic generation profiles reports lower mean Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) than the selected task-specific baselines for imputation and 16-fold super-resolution.
